subrules.name: 701.70a
subrules.rule: “Journey” means “Exile the top card of your library. That card becomes journeyed.”

subrules.name: 701.70b
subrules.rule: There is an inherent triggered ability associated with journeying. The full text of this ability is “Whenever a creature deals combat damage to one of its controller's opponents, if its controller owns any journeyed cards, the creature's controller puts a journeyed card they own into their hand.” This ability has no source and is controlled by the controller of the creature which dealt the damage that caused it to trigger. This is an exception to rule 113.8.

subrules.name: 701.70c
subrules.rule: Journeyed is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that the inherent triggered ability and other spells and abilities can identify. Only cards in exile can gain or have this designation. Once a card becomes journeyed, it stays journeyed until it leaves exile or becomes a new object (see rule 406.7). Journeyed is neither an ability nor part of the card's copiable values.

subrules.name: 701.71a
subrules.rule: To waste a permanent means to create a continuous effect. The permanent's name is changed to Wastes, it becomes a basic land, gains “{T}: Add {C},” and loses all other supertypes, card types, subtypes, and abilities.

subrules.name: 701.72a
subrules.rule: To add a card to your evil plan, look at the card, then exile it face down. Cards exiled this way are “in your evil plan.”

subrules.name: 701.72b
subrules.rule: A player may look at the cards exiled in their evil plan.

subrules.name: 701.72c
subrules.rule: Once each turn, a player may pay {7} as a sorcery to cast any of the cards in their evil plan without paying their mana costs. This is a special action. See rule 116.2a.

subrules.name: 701.73a
subrules.rule: Crystallize is a keyword action. “Crystallize” means “You may put a +1/+1 counter on a creature you control. If you don't, create a Treasure token.”

subrules.name: 701.74a
subrules.rule: Certain abilities instruct a permanent to “dare N.” Until end of turn, that permanent becomes legendary, a Rebel creature in addition to its other types, and has base power and toughness N/N.

subrules.name: 701.75a
subrules.rule: Bless is a keyword action. “You may bless [an object]” means “If this object's back face is a Blessing, create a token that's a copy of its back face and attach it to [object].”

subrules.name: 701.75b
subrules.rule:
If the back face of the object performing the bless object is not a Blessing, nothing will occur.
Example Bringer of Heliod’s Light says “When Bringer of Heliod’s Light enters, you may bless target creature.” If a non-double-faced permanent enters the battlefield as a copy of it, the ability will trigger, but no token will be created.

subrules.name: 701.76a
subrules.rule: Some abilities instruct a player to integrate a card or permanent. To do so, exile it, then for each card the object was represented by exiled this way, you may choose any nonland permanent.

subrules.name: 701.76b
subrules.rule: The term “integrated onto” describes the relationship between the card exiled by the integrate ability and the permanent chosen when the spell represented by that card resolves

subrules.name: 701.76c
subrules.rule: The exiled card remains integrated onto the chosen permanent as long as the integrated card remains exiled and the permanent remains on the battlefield. The card remains integrated onto that object even if it changes controller, as long as it remains on the battlefield.

subrules.name: 701.77a
subrules.rule: “Teach [a permanent] [keyword].” means “If that [permanent] has [keyword], put a +1/+1 counter on it. Otherwise, put a [keyword] counter on it.”

subrules.name: 701.78a
subrules.rule: Making a pledge is a keyword action. “Make a pledge” means “If you control a Clique, activate one of its pledge abilities without paying its activation cost. Otherwise, create one of the Clique tokens associated with one of the colors in this object's color identity as this spell or ability was put onto the stack.”

subrules.name: 701.78b
subrules.rule: The Clique tokens associated with white are Tiril Bureau, Penrath Insurgency, and Sillaman Laboratories.

subrules.name: 701.78c
subrules.rule: The Clique tokens associated with blue are Tiril Bureau, Hazakh Arsenal, and Sillaman Laboratories.

subrules.name: 701.78d
subrules.rule: The Clique tokens associated with black are Tiril Bureau, Hazakh Arsenal, and Vishanki Inc..

subrules.name: 701.78e
subrules.rule: The Clique tokens associated with red are Hazakh Arsenal, Vishanki Inc., and Penrath Insurgency.

subrules.name: 701.78f
subrules.rule: The Clique tokens associated with green are Vishanki Inc., Penrath Insurgency, and Sillaman Laboratories.

subrules.name: 701.78g
subrules.rule: There are no Clique tokens associated with colorless.

subrules.name: 701.79a
subrules.rule: Acclimate is a keyword action.

subrules.name: 701.79b
subrules.rule: As a permanent acclimates, its controller may reveal a Weather card they own from outside the game or in their graveyard and put it into their hand. If they don't, they put a +1/+1 counter on that permanent.

subrules.name: 701.79c
subrules.rule: If an effect instructs a player to acclimate, they may reveal a Weather card they own from outside the game or in their graveyard and put it into their hand. If they don't, they put a +1/+1 counter on a creature they control.

subrules.name: 701.80a
subrules.rule: To cache a card, exile it, then create a colorless Memory enchantment token with "{2}, Sacrifice this Memory: You may play the exiled card this turn." The exiled card becomes a cached card and gains "The player who controls the created Memory may look at this card in the exile zone."

subrules.name: 701.80b
subrules.rule: Some abilities instruct a player to cache a card face down. The same process occurs, except the player first looks at the card, then exiles it face down.

subrules.name: 701.80c
subrules.rule: If an effect instructs a player to cache multiple cards, those cards are cached one at a time.

subrules.name: 701.80d
subrules.rule: When a cached card is cast, it becomes a cached spell, even if it was cast by some method other than its associated Memory token.

subrules.name: 701.81a
subrules.rule: To run your next program, if you have no current program, your current program becomes Program A. Otherwise your current program moves to the next program: from A to B, from B to C, or from C to A. Then all Subroutines you control in your current program run (See 303.9, "Subroutines").

subrules.name: 701.83a
subrules.rule: To stitch X, a player may exile a creature card from their graveyard and an instant or sorcery card from their graveyard. If they do, they create an X/X blue Zombie creature token.

subrules.name: 701.83b
subrules.rule: The cards exiled with the stitch ability are "stitched with" the token. This designation has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that other effects can identify.

subrules.name: 701.83c
subrules.rule: Effects that occur when or as "you stitch a token" refer to creating a token with the stitch ability.

subrules.name: 701.83d
subrules.rule: An effect may allow a player to pay an alternate cost "to stitch". This alternate cost can be paid in place of exiling a creature card from their graveyard and an instant or sorcery card from their graveyard.

subrules.name: 702.195a
subrules.rule: Accomplice is a triggered ability. “Accomplice” means “Whenever another creature you control attacks, you may tap this creature.”

subrules.name: 702.195b
subrules.rule: A creature “becomes an accomplice to [a creature]” when the former creature is tapped as a result of a resolving accomplice ability that triggered from the latter creature's being declared as an attacker. The latter creature is also called the creature the former creature accompliced.

subrules.name: 702.196a
subrules.rule: Undercover is a static ability that functions in any zone from which you could play the card it's on, and the undercover effect works any time the card is face down. “Undercover [cost]” means “You may cast this card as a 2/2 face-down creature with no text, no name, no subtypes, and no mana cost by paying {3} rather than paying its mana cost.” (See rule 707, “Face-Down Spells and Permanents.”)

subrules.name: 702.196b
subrules.rule: To cast a card using its undercover ability, turn it face down. It becomes a 2/2 face-down creature card with no text, no name, no subtypes, and no mana cost. Any effects or prohibitions that would apply to casting a card with these characteristics (and not the face-up card's characteristics) are applied to casting this card. These values are the copiable values of that object's characteristics. (See rule 613, “Interaction of Continuous Effects,” and rule 706, “Copying Objects.”) Put it onto the stack (as a face-down spell with the same characteristics), and pay {3} rather than pay its mana cost. This follows the rules for paying alternative costs. You can use an undercover ability to cast a card from any zone from which you could normally play it. When the spell resolves, it enters the battlefield with the same characteristics the spell had. The undercover effect applies to the face-down object wherever it is, and it ends when the permanent is exiled or turned face up.

subrules.name: 702.196c
subrules.rule: If a face-down permanent that was cast for its undercover cost would die, instead its controller exiles it face down. No player looks at or reveals the card as it's exiled. This is an exception to rules 400.6 and 707.9. The player who exiled it may look at the exiled card and may play it for as long as it remains exiled, but can't play it face down this way. If the exiled card leaves exile, becomes a new object (see rule 406.7), its owner leaves the game, or the game ends, the card must be revealed to all players.

subrules.name: 702.196d
subrules.rule: See rule 707, “Face-Down Spells and Permanents,” for more information about how to cast cards with undercover.

subrules.name: 702.197a
subrules.rule: Experience is a triggered ability. “Experience” means “Whenever this creature attacks, if it has two or fewer +1/+1 counters on it, put a +1/+1 counter on it.”

subrules.name: 702.197b
subrules.rule: If a creature with experience has three or more +1/+1 counters on it as the ability tries to resolve, it will have no effect.

subrules.name: 702.198a
subrules.rule: “Harness” means “As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may tap an untapped creature you control. This spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is that creature's power.”

subrules.name: 702.198b
subrules.rule: The creature tapped this way “harnesses” that spell.

subrules.name: 702.199a
subrules.rule: Invoke appears on some double-faced cards. It represents a static abilities that functions while the card with invoke is in a player's graveyard. “Invoke (cost)” means “If you don't control a Totem creature, create a 0/0 colorless Totem creature token. Then put this card onto the battlefield transformed. Activate only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.199b
subrules.rule: If the transformed permanent has no legal targets, it will still enter the battlefield, then be put into its owner's graveyard (or exiled if it's a totemic permanent) the next time state-based effects are checked.

subrules.name: 702.200a
subrules.rule: Master is a triggered ability of some permanents.

subrules.name: 702.200b
subrules.rule: “Master of [name]” means “When this permanent enters, search your library for a card named [name], reveal it, put it into your hand, then shufle.”

subrules.name: 702.200c
subrules.rule: “Master of any [quality]” means “When this permanent enters, search your library for a [quality] card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shufle.”

subrules.name: 702.201a
subrules.rule: Unite is a triggered ability of some creatures. “Unite with [amount] creatures” means “Whenever this creatures attacks, if it has no +1/+1 counters on it, you may tap [amount] untapped creatures you control. If you do, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature.”

subrules.name: 702.201b
subrules.rule: A creature “unites creatures” whenever creatures are tapped as part of its unite ability.

subrules.name: 702.202a
subrules.rule: Coalesce appears on Revelation cards. It represents three static abilities: one that functions while the card is in a player's graveyard and two that function while the card is on the stack. “Coalesce (cost)” means “You may cast this card from your graveyard by paying (cost) rather than paying its mana cost” and “If the coalesce cost was paid, put this card onto the battlefield as a Horror creature. If this spell is a kindred, it also has each of this spell's creature types. If it would leave the battlefield, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else,” and “If the coalesce cost was paid, exile this card instead of putting it anywhere else anytime it would leave the stack except being put onto the battlefield with its coalesce ability.”

subrules.name: 702.202b
subrules.rule: A copy of a spell cast for its coalesce cost is unable to enter the battlefield, as a token or otherwise. The spell effect of the copy will still happen as normal.

subrules.name: 702.203a
subrules.rule: Propagate is a triggered ability. “Propagate N” means “When this permanent enters, you may put N +1/+1 counters on it. If you don’t, create N 0/1 colorless Eldrazi Spawn creature tokens with 'Sacrifice this creature: Add {C}.'”

subrules.name: 702.203b
subrules.rule: If a permanent has multiple instances of proagate, each triggers separately.

subrules.name: 702.204a
subrules.rule: Glory is a triggered ability. “Glory” means “When this creature dies while attacking, return it to the battlefield transformed.”

subrules.name: 702.204b
subrules.rule: The permanent will return under the control of whoever controlled triggered ability, usually whoever controlled the creature when it died.

subrules.name: 702.205a
subrules.rule: Endgame on a permanent represents a static ability. It means “Any time you control eight or more tapped permanents and you're not in your endgame, you're in your endgame for the rest of the game.”

subrules.name: 702.205b
subrules.rule: Endgame on an instant or sorcery spell represents a spell ability. It means “If you control eight or more tapped permanents and you're not in your endgame, you're in your endgame for the rest of the game.”

subrules.name: 702.205c
subrules.rule: Your endgame is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that other rules and effects can identify. Any number of players may be in their endgame at the same time.

subrules.name: 702.205d
subrules.rule: After a player enters their endgame, continuous effects are reapplied before the game checks to see if the game state or preceding events have matched any trigger conditions.

subrules.name: 702.206a
subrules.rule: Traverse is an activated ability of Rift cards. “Traverse N” means “Tap any number of untapped creatures you control with total power N or greater: This Rift is traversed. Sacrifice it. Activate this ability only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.206b
subrules.rule: Traversed is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that the Rift and other spells and abilities can identify.

subrules.name: 702.206c
subrules.rule: A creature “traverses a Rift” when it’s tapped to pay the cost to activate a Rift’s traverse ability.

subrules.name: 702.206d
subrules.rule: If an effect states that a creature “can’t traverse Rifts,” that creature can’t be tapped to pay the traverse cost of a Rift.

subrules.name: 702.207a
subrules.rule: Reflect is an ability found on the front face of some transforming double-faced cards (see rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards”). “Reflect [cost]” means “You may cast this card transformed from your graveyard by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost.” See rule 712.4b.

subrules.name: 702.207b
subrules.rule: A resolving transforming double-faced spell that was cast using its reflect ability enters the battlefield with its back face up.

subrules.name: 702.208a
subrules.rule: Reflected is an ability found on the back face of some transforming double-faced cards (see rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards”). “Reflected” means “If this permanent would leave the battlefield, exile it instead.”

subrules.name: 702.209a
subrules.rule: Tunneler is a static ability of some creatures. “Tunneler” means “As this creature enters, you may open the tunnels” and “As this creature becomes untapped, you may have it descend into the tunnels or exit the tunnels.”

subrules.name: 702.209b
subrules.rule: As a creature enters, if the tunnels are open, that creature's controller may have it descend into the tunnels.

subrules.name: 702.209c
subrules.rule: Creatures that are in the tunnels can only block and only be blocked by creatures that are in the tunnels.

subrules.name: 702.209d
subrules.rule: At the beginning of combat on each player's turn, if the tunnels are open and no creatures are in the tunnels, that player may close the tunnels.

subrules.name: 702.210a
subrules.rule: Maneuver is an ability found on some split cards. “Maneuver” means “If you cast this spell from your hand, exile it. As long as it remains exiled, you may cast it from exile.”

subrules.name: 702.211a
subrules.rule: Multitude is a keyword that represents a static ability and a triggered ability that function while the spell with multitude is on the stack. “Multitude (cost)” means “You may choose to pay (cost) rather than this spell's mana cost,” and “When you cast this spell, if you paid its multitude cost, copy it. If the spell has any targets, you may choose new targets for the copy.”

subrules.name: 702.212a
subrules.rule: Indulgence is a static ability found on some permanents.

subrules.name: 702.212b
subrules.rule: As a player's end step begins, if they control any permanents with indulgence and they either gained 3 or more life or drew two or more cards this turn, that player “indulges.” Indulges is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that spells and abilities can identify.

subrules.name: 702.213a
subrules.rule: Favored is a triggered ability. “Favored” means “At the beginning of each of your combats, if you haven't chosen a Champion this combat, you may choose a nonlegendary creature you control to be your Champion. As long as that creature remains on the battlefield, it gets +1/+1, becomes legendary, and its name becomes The Champion.

subrules.name: 702.213b
subrules.rule: Some effects refer to “your Champion.” This means “a permanent you control named The Champion.”

subrules.name: 702.213c
subrules.rule: The Champion will continue to get +1/+1, be legendary, and be named the Champion as long as it remains on the battlefield, but it will only be considered “your Champion” for the player that currently controls it, regardless of if they chose it as their Champion or not.

subrules.name: 702.214a
subrules.rule: Spellcharge is a triggered ability. “Spellcharge N” means “At the beginning of combat on your turn, if you've spend at least N mana to cast spells this turn, you may have spellcharge this permanent and have it become a creature in addition to its other types until end of turn.”

subrules.name: 702.215a
subrules.rule: Wander appears on some permanent cards. “Wander (cost)” means “You may cast this permanent from the battlefield for (cost).” Casting a spell using its wander ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.216a
subrules.rule: Cybersoul is an activated ability. “Cybersoul [Cost]” means “[Cost]: Transform this permanent. For each generic mana in this ability's total cost, you may tap an untapped artifact you control rather than pay that mana. Activate only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.217a
subrules.rule: Solidarity is a triggered ability. “Solidarity” means “Whenever you attack and there are six or more different creature types among attacking creatures, if this is the first solidarity ability you control that has resolved this turn, create a Solidarity token.” See rule 111.10aa.

subrules.name: 702.218a
subrules.rule: A pledge ability is a special kind of activated ability, written as "Pledge — [Activated ability]." Pledge has no rules meaning other than to be a designation other effects can identify.

subrules.name: 702.219a
subrules.rule: “Surface [cost]” means “You may cast a copy of this card from your graveyard by paying [cost] and exiling this card from your graveyard rather than paying its mana cost as long as there are six or more other cards in your graveyard.” Casting a spell using its surface ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.219b
subrules.rule:
Surface abilities may have additional text after their cost. This text only applies if that specific surface cost is being paid.
Example: Entangled Fossil says "Surface {4}{G}{G}. Entangled Fossil surfaces transformed." and "{G}, Sacrifice Entangled Fossil: Target card in your graveyard gains surface until end of turn. The surface cost is equal to its mana cost." Sacrificing an Entangled Fossil targeting a second copy will allow it to be cast for Surface {G}, but it will not surface transformed if cast this way.

subrules.name: 702.219c
subrules.rule: An ability that reads "[This permanent] surfaces transformed" means the copy created by the surface ability will be cast transformed. The surfaced card and permanent remain a copy of a double-faced card, and so maintains its mana value, and is able to transform back if instructed to by another effect.

subrules.name: 702.219d
subrules.rule: A spell or permanent "surfaces" or "surfaced" if that spell or the spell that became that permanent as it resolved was cast from a graveyard with a surface ability.

subrules.name: 702.219e
subrules.rule: An ability that reads "[This permanent] surfaces with [one or more of a kind of counter]" means "If this permanent surfaces, it enters with [those counters]"

subrules.name: 702.219f
subrules.rule: An ability that reads "[This permanent] surfaces with [ability]" means "If this permanent surfaced, it has [ability]."

subrules.name: 702.220a
subrules.rule: A flow ability is a special kind of activated ability. "Flow — [Cost]: [Effect]" means "[Cost]: [Effect]. For each generic mana in this ability's total cost, you may tap an untapped creature you control rather than pay that mana."

subrules.name: 702.221a
subrules.rule: Revered is a static ability. "Revered" means "Each other creature you control that has one or more counters on it has the abilities printed below this one." Cards with revered have one or more abilities printed after the revered ability. Some cards with revered also have abilities printed before the revered ability, which are not granted to other creatures.

subrules.name: 702.222a
subrules.rule: Time loop is a keyword found on some Saga cards. "Time loop" means "As this Saga's final chapter ability resolves, remove all lore counters from it." If lore counters are removed this way, the Saga will not be sacrificed as it normally would be (see rule 714.4).

subrules.name: 702.223a
subrules.rule: Chant is a static ability that functions while a card is in your hand. “Chant [cost]” means “You may exile this card from your hand as you cast an instant or sorcery spell. If you do, that spell gains the text found within square brackets in this card’s rules text and you pay [cost] as an additional cost to cast that spell. You may cast this card as long as this card remains exiled.” Paying a card’s chant cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.223b
subrules.rule: Some effect may allow a player to "add the chants" of cards to spells they cast. To do so, they choose the cards with chant that will add their chants. The spell gains the text found within the square brackets in those card's rules text, and that player pays [cost] as an additional cost to cast that spell. The chanting creatures will not be exiled.

subrules.name: 702.223c
subrules.rule: You can’t choose to use a chant ability if you can’t make the required choices (targets, etc.) for that card’s rules text. If you’re chanting more than one card onto a spell, exile them all at once and choose the order in which their effects will happen. The effects of the main spell must happen first.

subrules.name: 702.223d
subrules.rule: The spell has the characteristics of the main spell, plus the rules text found in the square brackets of each of the chanting cards. This is a text-changing effect (see rule 612, “Text-Changing Effects”). The spell doesn’t gain any other characteristics (name, mana cost, color, supertypes, card types, subtypes, etc.) of the chanting cards. Text gained by the spell that refers to a card by name refers to the spell on the stack, not the card from which the text was copied.

subrules.name: 702.223e
subrules.rule: Choose targets for the added text normally (see rule 601.2c). Note that a spell with one or more targets won’t resolve if all of its targets are illegal on resolution.

subrules.name: 702.223f
subrules.rule: The spell loses any chant changes once it leaves the stack for any reason.

subrules.name: 702.224a
subrules.rule: Decoy is a triggered ability that creates a delayed triggered ability. “Decoy” means “Whenever this creature attacks, create a tapped and attacking token that’s a copy of it, except it's a 1/1 Illusion instead of its other creature types.” and “Exile that token at the beginning of the next end step.”

subrules.name: 702.224b
subrules.rule: If a creature has multiple instances of decoy, each triggers separately.

subrules.name: 702.224c
subrules.rule: If a replacement effect causes the decoy ability to create multiple tokens, they will be exiled by the delayed trigger as well.

subrules.name: 702.225a
subrules.rule: Rapture is a triggered ability. "Rapture" means "When this creature dies, return it to the battlefield with a haze counter on it. As long as it has a haze counter on it, it loses all abilities and can't block."

subrules.name: 702.226a
subrules.rule: Reprieve is a static ability. “Reprieve” means “As this creature enters, you may return a creature you control without reprieve to its owner's hand.”

subrules.name: 702.226b
subrules.rule: A creature with reprieve “reprieves a creature” when its controller returns a creature to a player's hand with the ability.

subrules.name: 702.227a
subrules.rule: Syzygy represents two static abilities, one that functions while the card with syzygy is on the stack, and the other on the battlefield. "Syzygy" means "For each generic mana in this spell's total cost, you may tap an untapped creature you control rather than pay that mana" and "For each generic mana in the total cost of this permanent's abilities, you may tap another untapped creature you control rather than pay that mana."

subrules.name: 702.228a
subrules.rule: Possess is a triggered ability. "Possess" means "When this creature dies, if it was a nontoken creature as it left the battlefield, you may return it to the battlefield as an Aura enchantment with enchant creature attached to target creature."

subrules.name: 702.228b
subrules.rule: If there is no legal target for the possess ability, the card with possess will remain in its owner's graveyard.

subrules.name: 702.228c
subrules.rule: When returning as an Aura, the card will lose all its types, but will not lose any of its abilities. If the permanent becomes a non-Aura creature, its possess ability may trigger again.

subrules.name: 702.229a
subrules.rule: Pursuit represents a static ability that functions while the card with pursuit is in a player's graveyard. "Pursuit [cost]" means "You may cast a copy of this card from your graveyard by paying [cost], sacrificing a nonland permanent, and exiling this card from your graveyard rather than paying its mana cost." Casting a spell using its pursuit ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

Each Campaign card has a striated text box containing a number of strategy symbols. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.
A strategy symbol is a keyword ability that represents one or more triggered abilities referred to as strategy abilities.

subrules.name: 740.2a
subrules.rule: A strategy symbol includes a number of flags, indicated here as “{f}.”

subrules.name: 740.2b
subrules.rule: “{f}, {f}—[Effect]” means the same as “{f}—[Effect]” and “{f}—[Effect].”

subrules.name: 740.2c
subrules.rule: Whenever a Campaign's controller attacks, they put a strategy counter on the Campaign.

subrules.name: 740.2d
subrules.rule: As a strategy counter is put on a Campaign, its controller triggers a strategy ability of that Campaign of their choice. That ability can't be triggered this way again as long as that counter remains on the Campaign.

subrules.name: 740.2e
subrules.rule: A Campaign’s final strategy number is the total number of strategy abilities it has. If a Campaign somehow has no strategy abilities, its final strategy number is 0.
Camapaigns use strategy counters to track their progress.

If the number of strategy counters on a Campaign permanent is greater than or equal to its final strategy number, and it isn't the source of a strategy ability that has triggered but not yet left the stack, that Campaigns's controller sacrifices it. This state-based action doesn't use the stack.

Each Policy card is a double-faced card. The front face has a striated textbox containing a number of policy symbols. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its typeline is along the bottom of the card. The back face is a standard Magic card.
A policy symbol is a keyword ability that represents a static ability that allows a player to take a special action.

subrules.name: 741.2a
subrules.rule: A policy symbol includes a quill icon, indicated here as {ql}.

subrules.name: 741.2b
subrules.rule: "{ql}—[Condition]" means "Any time you could cast a sorcery, you may mark this condition if [condition] and if no player has marked a policy symbol of this permanent this turn. When you do, if all of this permanent's policy abilities are marked, transform this permanent."

subrules.name: 741.2c
subrules.rule: "{ql}, {ql}—[Condition]" means the same as "{ql}—[Condition]" and "{ql}—[Condition]."

subrules.name: 741.2d
subrules.rule: A policy symbol may be marked even if it is already marked.

subrules.name: 741.2e
subrules.rule: A condition being marked has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that spells and abilities can identify. Once a permanent's condition becomes marked, it stays marked until it leaves the battlefield or transforms as a result of its policy symbol (see rule R741.2b). The marked designation is neither an ability nor part of the permanent’s copiable values.

Each Operation card has a striated text box containing one or more operation ability bars. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the left side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.

An operation ability bar is a keyword aility that represents a static ability. An operation ability bar includes a condition. Any abilities printed within the same text box section as the operation ability bar are part of its static ability.

subrules.name: 742.2a
subrules.rule: "N Defense — [Abilities]" means "As long as this permanent has N or fewer defense counters on it, it has [abilities]." An Operation "reaches this stage" as one or more counters are removed from it while it has more than N counters on it, resulting in it having N or fewer counters on it. This may happen several times, but will only trigger abilities that check "first reaches this stage" the first time it occurs.

subrules.name: 742.2b
subrules.rule: "Defeated — [Abilities]" means "As long as this permanent has no defense counters on it, it has [abilities]."

Any ability printed on an Operation card that isn’t preceded by a class level bar is treated normally. In particular, the Operation has the ability printed in its top text box section at all times. That ability may affect the game if it’s a static ability, it may trigger if it’s a triggered ability, and it can be activated if it’s an activated ability.
Discharge cards have a two-part card frame, with a smaller frame inset within their text box.

The text that appears in the inset frame on the right defines alternative characteristics that the object may have while it’s a spell. The card’s normal characteristics appear as usual, although with a smaller text box on the left.

subrules.name: 743.2a
subrules.rule: The inset frame of a discharge card is called a “Discharge spell.” If a rule or effect refers to a card, spell, or permanent that has a Discharge spell, it refers to an object for which these alternative characteristics exist, even if the object currently doesn’t use them.

subrules.name: 743.2b
subrules.rule: The existence and values of these alternative characteristics are part of the object’s copiable values.

subrules.name: 743.2c
subrules.rule: Although discharge cards are printed with multiple sets of characteristics, each discharge card is only one card. For example, a player who has drawn or discarded a discharge card has drawn or discarded one card, not two.
Discharge cards can’t be cast using the alternative characteristics found within their inset frames. Rather, these characteristics are used to define characteristics of copies which may be cast.

subrules.name: 743.3a
subrules.rule: As a permanent with a Discharge spell enters or a permanent gains a Discharge, its controller creates a copy of the Discharge spell in exile, except that copy has only the characteristics of that permanent’s Discharge spell, ignoring other exceptions to the copying process that apply to that permanent. Those characteristics become the copy’s normal characteristics. This copy remains in exile for as long as the permanent remains on the battlefield and has the Discharge spell. This is an exception to rule 704.5e. For as long as the copy remains in exile, the permanent’s controller may cast the copy by removing a counter from the permanent in addition to paying the spell's other costs.

subrules.name: 743.3b
subrules.rule: If a Discharge spell is copied, the copy is also a Discharge spell. Any rule or effect that refers to a spell cast as a Discharge spell refers to the copy as well.
In every zone, a discharge card has only its normal characteristics.
If an effect instructs a player to choose a card name and the player wants to choose a discharge card’s alternative name, the player may do so.

subrules.name: 701.69a
subrules.rule: Adjudicate is a keyword action that means “Create a white Aura enchantment token with enchant creature and 'Sacrifice this token: Untap enchanted creature' and attach it to target creature.”

subrules.name: 701.69b
subrules.rule: If the token can't be attached to the target creature, for example if it has protection from enchantments, the token will never enter the battlefield.

subrules.name: 701.69c
subrules.rule: Adjudicate type is a variant of the adjudicate action. “Adjudicate [type]” means “Create a white Aura enchantment token with enchant [type] and 'Sacrifice this token: Untap enchanted permanent' and attach it to target [type] permanent.”

subrules.name: 701.70a
subrules.rule: Certain spells and abilities cause a player to catalyze. The next spell that player casts this turn costs (1) less to cast.

subrules.name: 701.70b
subrules.rule: Multiple instances of catalyze stack, but will all apply to the same spell, even if the spell costs less than the number of active catalyzes.

subrules.name: 701.71a
subrules.rule: Idolize is an keyword action that means “Create a colorless Idol artifact token with '(1), Sacrifice this artifact: Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature. Activate only as a sorcery.'”

subrules.name: 701.71b
subrules.rule: An Idol can still be sacrificed if it somehow stops being an artifact.

subrules.name: 701.72a
subrules.rule: Invigorate N is a keyword action that means “Choose a creature you control with the least power or tied for the least power among creatures you control. Put N +1/+1 counters on that creature.”

subrules.name: 701.72b
subrules.rule: Conditional invigorate is a variant of the invigorate ability. “Invigorate N [condition]” means “Choose a creature you control with the least power or tied for the least power among [condition] creatures yo control. Put a +1/+1 counter on that creature.”

subrules.name: 701.73a
subrules.rule: Purge is a keyword action that means “Exile two cards that share a card type from graveyards. If you exile two cards this way, draw a card.”

subrules.name: 701.74a
subrules.rule: To submerge a card, exile it face up, then put it onto the battlefield face down under its owner's control as a 2/2 face-down creature card with no text, no name, no subtypes, and no mana cost. That permanent is a submerged permanent as long as it remains face down. The effect defining its characteristics works while the card is face down and ends when it’s turned face up.

subrules.name: 701.74b
subrules.rule: Unlike manifest, a submerged card can not turn face up again on its own.

subrules.name: 701.75a
subrules.rule: To post a bounty on a permanent means to put a bounty counter on that permanent. For as long as that permanent has a bounty counter on it, it has “When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, each opponent draws a card.”

subrules.name: 701.75b
subrules.rule: A new triggered ability is gained each time a bounty is placed on a permanent.

subrules.name: 701.75c
subrules.rule: The permanent will only gain the ability once per time a bounty is posted, even if it would get more than one bounty counter from it, such as through Doubling Season.

subrules.name: 701.75d
subrules.rule: If some bounty counters are removed but not all of them, the permanent will still have the ability as many times as a bounty was posted on it.

subrules.name: 701.76a
subrules.rule: To arm a creature, create a colorless Equipment artifact token with “Equipped creature gets +1/+0” and equip {2}, then attach that token to that creature.

subrules.name: 701.76b
subrules.rule: If the creature that is being armed can't be equipped by the Equipment token (for example, it isn't on the battlefield anymore), the token is created but isn't attached to anything.

subrules.name: 701.77a
subrules.rule: “Nourish N” means “You may put N +1/+1 counters on this permanent. If you don't, create N 1/1 white Citizen creature tokens.”

subrules.name: 701.78a
subrules.rule: Abound is a keyword action. “Abound” means “You may cast a spell from your hand with a lesser mana value than this spell or permanent without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 701.78b
subrules.rule: If an triggered or activated ability instructs you to abound, use the mana value of the source of that ability to determine the mana value. If the ability somehow doesn't have a source, its mana value is 0 and you will be unable to cast a spell with a lesser mana value.

subrules.name: 701.79a
subrules.rule: Journey is a keyword action. To journey, exile the top card of your library face up and it becomes journeyed.

subrules.name: 701.79b
subrules.rule: There is an inherent triggered ability associated with owning journeyed cards in exile. This triggered ability has no source and is controlled by the player whose creature triggered it. The full text of this ability is “Whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to an opponent, put a journeyed card you own from exile into your hand.”

subrules.name: 701.79c
subrules.rule: The triggered ability will trigger once for each creature that dealt combat damage, regardless of how many journeyed cards that player owns in exile.

subrules.name: 701.80a
subrules.rule: Conjure is a keyword action. “Conjure (number) cards named (name) to (zone)” means “Put (number) cards named (name) into (zone).”

subrules.name: 701.80b
subrules.rule: “Conjure (number) of a random (quality) card to (zone)” means “Put (number) cards of a single (quality) card chosen at random into (zone).”

subrules.name: 701.80c
subrules.rule: “Conjure a random (quality) card to (zone) (number) times” means “Repeat this process (number) times. Put a (quality) card chosen at random into (zone)”

subrules.name: 701.80d
subrules.rule: To “conjure a duplicate” of an object, conjure the card that has the same name, alternative name, interchangeable name, or name of back face as that object. If such a card does not exist, for example, it is a token named after its types, no card will be conjured.

subrules.name: 701.80e
subrules.rule: Conjured cards are not moved from any zone or a player's sideboard.

subrules.name: 701.80f
subrules.rule: Conjured cards are cards and not tokens, even if they are represented by token or checklists cards.

subrules.name: 701.80g
subrules.rule: Conjured cards are known to all players, even if they are conjured to a hidden zone.

subrules.name: 701.80h
subrules.rule: The owner of a conjured card is the player who conjured it, regardless of who controlled the effect that caused that player to conjure it.

subrules.name: 701.80i
subrules.rule: When a game ends, cards that were conjured during that game are removed from decks.

subrules.name: 701.80j
subrules.rule: When a game is restarted, cards that were conjured during that game remain in decks.

subrules.rule: Harmonize is a keyword action. “Harmonize” means “Choose up to one harmony ability of a permanent you control.” Choosing an ability this way causes that ability to trigger.

subrules.rule: “Germinate” means “You may put a +1/+1 counter on a creature. If you don't, create a 1/1 green Saproling creature token.”

subrules.name: 701.83a
subrules.rule: To profit, create a colorless Gold artifact token with “Sacrifice this artifact: Add one mana of any color.”

subrules.name: 701.84a
subrules.rule: To substantiate a card, put it onto the battlefield face down under your control as a 2/2 face-down creature card with no text, no name, no subtypes, and no mana cost. subrules.rule: If an effect such as Doubling Season causes you to create more than one token, all the tokens created by the aetherize action will be exiled.

subrules.rule: Torment is a keyword action. The tormented player loses 3 life unless they discard a card or sacrifice a nonland permanent.

subrules.rule: A voyaging permanent “returns from voyage” when it phases in.

subrules.rule: Upgrade is a keyword action and modal ability. “upgrade a permanent. [bulleted list]” means “Choose one that's not a kind of counter this permanent has on it. Put a counter of that kind on this permanent. [bulleted list].”

subrules.rule: Honoring or condemning a permanent has no rules meaning, and only acts a designation that spells and abilities can identify.

subrules.rule: Dynamizing a permanent that is already dynamized is redundant.

subrules.rule: If a permanent has multiple instances of alpha, each works separately.

subrules.name: 702.193c
subrules.rule: If an alpha permanent loses its +1/+1 counter, it's still alpha and can still only attack alone.

subrules.rule: A creature with distorted can still only block creatures without distorted if it is untapped.

subrules.name: 702.197b
subrules.rule: This ability will trigger even if the permanent is not a creature when it is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.

subrules.rule: If a creature with experience has three or more +1/+1 counters on it as the ability tries to resolve, it will have no effect.

subrules.name: 702.199a

subrules.rule: The fabled ability is linked to an ability printed on its front face that targets one or more objects that can be legally enchanted by its back face. If there are multiple possible targets, one is chosen as the spell with Fable resolves.

subrules.rule: If the targeted permanent or player is an illegal target for the Aura side of a card with fabled, such as a creature with protection from enchantments, the card with fabled will not enter the battlefield and instead be put directly into its owner's graveyard from the stack.

subrules.rule: Cards with this ability have the subtype Inscription.

subrules.rule: If the triggered ability of mirage is countered, it will not trigger again.

subrules.name: 702.203a
subrules.rule: Motivate is a trigged ability. “Motivate N” means “When this creature enters, you may put N +1/+1 counters on target creature with power less than this creature's power.”

subrules.name: 702.203b
subrules.rule: A creature with motivate “motivates a creature” and that creature “becomes motivated” when the controller of the motivate ability puts +1/+1 counters on a creature as that ability resolves.

subrules.name: 702.204a
subrules.rule: Prophecy is a keyword that represents a static ability linked to a triggered ability. “Prophecy (cost)” means “As you reveal this card from a hidden zone, you may exile it if you haven't exiled any cards with their prophecy ability this turn.” and “When you exile this card with its prophecy ability, you may cast it for (cost) rather than paying its mana cost as long as it remains exiled.”

subrules.name: 702.204b
subrules.rule:
When a card with prophecy is revealed, any relevant information about it is retained, but the card is exiled and becomes a new object.
Example Cursed Scroll will know the name of a card with prophecy, but it can't be put into a Fact or Fiction pile or chosen during the resolution of Gifts Ungiven.

subrules.name: 702.204c
subrules.rule: A card can't be cast for its prophecy cost if it was exiled by an effect other than its prophecy ability.

subrules.name: 702.205a
subrules.rule: Reprise is a static ability that functions while a card with reprise is in your graveyard. “Reprise (cost)” means “You may exile exactly one card with reprise from your graveyard as you cast an instant or sorcery spell. If you exile this card this way, copy this card's text box onto that spell and pay (cost) as an additional cost to cast that spell.”

subrules.name: 702.205b
subrules.rule: You can't choose to reprise a card if you can't make the required choices, such as targets, for that card's instructions.

subrules.name: 702.205c
subrules.rule: You can't ever exile two or more cards with reprise for a single spell.

subrules.name: 702.206a
subrules.rule: Reverberate is a keyword that represents a static ability and a triggered ability that function while the spell with reverberate is on the stack. “Reverberate (cost)” means “As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may pay (cost),” and “When you cast this spell, if you paid its reverberate cost, copy it. If the spell has any targets, you may choose new targets for the copy.”

subrules.name: 702.206b
subrules.rule: A spell is “reverberated” if it's a copy and it has reverberate.

subrules.name: 702.207a
subrules.rule: Revive is an activated ability that functions while the card with revive is in a graveyard. “Revive (cost)” means “(cost), Exile this card from your graveyard: Create a token that’s a copy of this card, except it has no mana cost. Activate this ability only any time you could cast a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.207b
subrules.rule: Revive will create a token that's a copy of the card as it was in the graveyard, rather than it is in exile.

subrules.name: 702.208a
subrules.rule: Shimmer is a triggered ability that may create one or more delayed triggered abilities. “Shimmer” means “Whenever this creature attacks, create a tapped and attacking token that’s a copy of it.” and “Exile that token at the beginning of the end step.”

subrules.name: 702.208b
subrules.rule: If a creature has multiple instances of shimmer, each triggers separately.

subrules.name: 702.208c
subrules.rule: The delayed trigger will retrigger at every end step. If the trigger is countered, or avoided by ending the turn, the token will remain on the battlefield and the ability will trigger on the next end step.

subrules.name: 702.208d
subrules.rule: Shimmer will only exile tokens created by its ability. Replacement effects such as Doubling Season cause shimmer to create two tokens, and both will be exiled. Effects that create a copy of those tokens, such as populate, will create a token will not attempt to be exiled every end step.

subrules.name: 702.208e
subrules.rule: If shimmer creates multiple tokens, each one will have its own end step exile trigger.

subrules.name: 702.209a
subrules.rule: Trial is a static ability that functions while a spell with trial is on the stack. “Trial N” means “As you cast this spell, an opponent of your choice may pay N life. If that player doesn't, they fail the trial.”

subrules.name: 702.209b
subrules.rule: Trials are paid or failed after targets have been chosen.

subrules.name: 702.209c
subrules.rule: Objects with trial have conditional effects that check “if the trial was failed,” this condition is true if the opponent chosen as a result of the trial ability didn't pay life as specified by the object's trial ability.

subrules.name: 702.210a
subrules.rule: Winnow is a static ability.

subrules.name: 702.210b
subrules.rule: Damage dealt to a creature with winnow causes that creature’s controller, or its owner if it has no controller, to lose that much life (in addition to any other results that damage causes). See rule 119.3

subrules.name: 702.210c
subrules.rule: Multiple instances of winnow on the same object are redundant.

subrules.name: 702.211a
subrules.rule: Kindle is an activated ability that functions while the card with kindle is in a graveyard. “Kindle X—(cost)” means “(cost), Exile this card from your graveyard: Create X 1/1 colorless Elemental creature tokens. Activate this ability only any time you could cast a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.212a
subrules.rule: Paranoia is a static ability linked to a triggered ability that functions while the card with paranoia is in a player's hand or on the stack. “Paranoia (cost)” means “You may reveal this card from your hand as a permanent you control leaves the battlefield. When you reveal this card this way, you may cast it by paying (cost) rather than its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.212b
subrules.rule: Casting a spell with paranoia ignores all normal timing restrictions for the spell. Effects can still prevent players from casting the spell or increase the mana cost to cast it.

subrules.name: 702.212c
subrules.rule: The triggered ability that allows you to cast a spell for its paranoia cost can be countered.

subrules.name: 702.212d
subrules.rule: If a spell is cast for its paranoia cost, other alternate mana costs can't be paid, but other additional costs can be.

subrules.name: 702.212e
subrules.rule: If a creature leaves the battlefield as part of a cost, unless it was to pay for a mana ability, paranoia will trigger before that spell or ability resolves.

subrules.name: 702.213a
subrules.rule: Engage is a static ability of some creatures. “Engage” means “This creature must be blocked each combat if able.”

subrules.name: 702.213b
subrules.rule:
This gets difficult when paired with menace. If there are multiple requirements on how creatures can block, the maximum amount of requirements must be obeyed.
Example: Untouched Duelist has engage and menace. You attack with an Untouched Duelist and two creatures with engage. Your opponent has two creatures. Blocking only the Untouched Duelist would leave two unfilled requirements, while blocking the other two engage creatures would leave one unfilled requirement, so the other two engage creatures must be blocked.

subrules.name: 702.214a
subrules.rule: Heretic is a triggered ability of some creatures. “Heretic” means “Whenever you cast a spell that doesn't share a color with this creature, this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.”

subrules.name: 702.214b
subrules.rule: Heretic only checks the color of the creature and the spell when the spell is cast. If either changes color afterwards, it will be too late to gain or negate the effect.

subrules.name: 702.214c
subrules.rule: Colorless spells will always trigger heretic, because they don't share a color with anything.

subrules.name: 702.215a
subrules.rule: Primal is a static ability that functions while the spell with primal is on the stack. “Primal (cost)” means “During your turn, you may cast this spell for (cost) rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If you do, casting this spell also counts as playing a land.”

subrules.name: 702.215b
subrules.rule: The spell with primal is still cast. It is not a special action, it only counts as playing a land when determining if a player can play a land this turn.

subrules.name: 702.215c
subrules.rule: A spell can be cast for its primal cost at any point during a player's turn, as long as the number of lands that player can play this turn is greater than the number of lands they have already played this turn, even if timing restrictions would normally prevent playing a land. This means a spell may be cast for its primal cost during its owner's upkeep or end step, but not during another player's turn, or during a turn where lands can't be played.

subrules.name: 702.215d
subrules.rule: Additional land plays allow you to play additional cards for their primal cost.

subrules.name: 702.216a
subrules.rule: Deception is an activated ability that functions only while the card with deception is in a player's hand. “Deception (cost)” means “(cost), Reveal this card from your hand, Return an unblocked attacking creature you control to its owner’s hand: Put this card onto the battlefield from your hand tapped and attacking.”

subrules.name: 702.216b
subrules.rule: The card with deception remains revealed from the time the ability is announced until the ability leaves the stack.

subrules.name: 702.216c
subrules.rule: A deception ability may be activated only while a creature on the battlefield is unblocked (after blockers are declared). The creature with deception is put onto the battlefield unblocked. It will be attacking the same player or planeswalker as the creature that was returned to its owner's hand.

subrules.name: 702.217a
subrules.rule: Quickdraw is a static ability linked to a triggered ability that functions while the card with quickdraw is in a player's hand or on the stack. “Quickdraw (cost)” means “You may reveal this card from your hand as a creature you control blocks or becomes blocked. When you reveal this card this way, you may cast it by paying (cost) rather than its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.217b
subrules.rule: Casting a spell with quickdraw ignores all normal timing restrictions for the spell. Effects can still prevent players from casting the spell or increase the mana cost to cast it.

subrules.name: 702.217c
subrules.rule: The triggered ability that allows you to cast a spell for its quickdraw cost can be countered.

subrules.name: 702.217d
subrules.rule: If a spell is cast for its quickdraw cost, other alternate mana costs can't be paid, but other additional costs can be.

subrules.name: 702.218a
subrules.rule: Vision is a triggered ability of some permanents. “Vision” means “When this permanent or another creature you control enters, reveal the top card of your library. Then you may put that card into your graveyard.”

subrules.name: 702.218b
subrules.rule: Cards that are revealed this way are “envisioned” by the source of the vision ability that revealed them.

subrules.name: 702.218c
subrules.rule: Putting the card into your graveyard has no effect on if the card is envisioned or not.

subrules.name: 702.218d
subrules.rule: Type vision is a variant of the vision ability. “[Type] vision” means “When this permanent or another [type] you control enters, reveal the top card of your library. Then you may put that card into your graveyard.”

subrules.name: 702.219a
subrules.rule: Archive is a static ability of Study enchantments. “Archive X” means “As this permanent enters, shuffle the top X cards of your starting library into an additional, face up, library.”

subrules.name: 702.219b
subrules.rule: The additional library is referred to as “the archived library” by the Study with the archive ability that created it.

subrules.name: 702.219c
subrules.rule: Whenever state-based actions are checked, if a Study enchantment has an archived library of zero cards, its controller sacrifices it.

subrules.name: 702.219d
subrules.rule: If a card would be put into an archived library, that card is put in that library face up.

subrules.name: 702.219e
subrules.rule: If a Study card with archive leaves the battlefield, the archived library remains, but is no longer affected by any effects the Study provided.

subrules.name: 702.219f
subrules.rule: Cards are not revealed when they are put into a face up library. Cards can still become revealed even though the cards are already visible.

subrules.name: 702.219g
subrules.rule: If another player gains control of a Study, they will control any effects of the Study, but will not own the archived library. This means cards from the archived library can't go into that player's hand, graveyard, or library, and cards that player owns can't be put into the archived library. Effects of the Study may still allow them to manipulate or play the cards in that library.

subrules.name: 702.219h
subrules.rule: “Your archived libraries” refers to each of your additional libraries that is currently the archived library of a Study on the battlefield. A library still counts as one of your archived libraries if you no longer control the Study, as long as the same object has remained on the battlefield.

subrules.name: 702.220a
subrules.rule: Cadence is a triggered ability of some creatures. “Cadence” means “Whenever you cast a spell, if its mana value is greater than this creature's power, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature.”

subrules.name: 702.220b
subrules.rule: If a permanent with cadence isn't a creature, the cadence ability will trigger whenever you cast a spell with mana value greater than 0.

subrules.name: 702.221a
subrules.rule: Orchestrate represents a static ability of a card in your hand that creates a delayed triggered ability. “Orchestrate (cost)” means “At any time you could cast a sorcery, you may pay (cost) and exile this card from your hand. If you do, when you next resolve a spell, cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.221b
subrules.rule: Exiling a card for its orchestrate cost is a special action and can't be countered.

subrules.name: 702.221c
subrules.rule: If the triggered ability created by orchestrate is countered, the card will remain in exile and the ability allowing you to cast it won't trigger anymore.

matched_card_names: Reytali, Song of the Sand//Reytali of Endless Muses

subrules.name: 702.222a
subrules.rule: Recite represents a static ability that functions while the card with recite is in a graveyard, a triggered ability that functions on the battlefield, and a static ability that functions on the battlefield. “Recite (cost)” means “You may cast this card from your graveyard by paying (cost) rather than paying its mana cost.”, “When this permanent enters, if its recite cost was paid, its controller exiles it.”, and “If this creature would leave the battlefield, if its recite cost was paid, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else.” Paying a card's recite cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs.

subrules.name: 702.223a
subrules.rule: Spirited is a triggered ability. “Spirited” means “When this permanent enters, you may activate one of its abilities without paying that ability's cost.”

subrules.name: 702.223b
subrules.rule: If a creature has spirited, its activated abilities whose cost includes the tap symbol or the untap symbol can be activated by its spirited ability even if that creature hasn’t been controlled by that player continuously since their most recent turn began.

subrules.name: 702.223c
subrules.rule: The ability that will be activated is chosen as the spirited ability resolves.

subrules.name: 702.223d
subrules.rule: Multiple instances of spirited trigger separately.

subrules.name: 702.224a
subrules.rule: Embody is a static ability of Persona Auras. It means “Enchanted creature is a copy of this Persona except for its types, supertypes, and subtypes.”

subrules.name: 702.225a
subrules.rule: Harvest represents a static ability that functions while the spell with harvest is on the stack. “Harvest” means “As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may tap any number of untapped creatures you control. This spell costs less to cast, where X is the total power of creatures tapped this way.” Paying a spell's harvest cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h.

subrules.name: 702.225b
subrules.rule: You choose which creatures you will tap as you choose to pay a spell's harvest cost, and you tap those creatures as you pay the total cost.

subrules.name: 702.226a
subrules.rule: Puzzlebox represents two abilities, a static ability that functions as a conspiracy card with puzzlebox is put into the command zone, and a static ability that functions while the conspiracy is face up in the command zone. “Puzzlebox” means “As you put this conspiracy card into the command zone, put a card you own from outside the game into the command zone face down and locked” and “As this puzzlebox becomes unlocked, turn the locked card face up.”

subrules.name: 702.227a
subrules.rule: Sleight is a static ability that functions while a spell with sleight is being cast. “Sleight” means “You may cast this spell as though it had flash if you pay more to cast it.

subrules.name: 702.227b
subrules.rule: The spell with sleight will not actually gain flash, you will just be able to cast it as though it did.

subrules.name: 702.228a
subrules.rule: Mark is a triggered ability of some creatures. “Mark” means “Whenever this creature attacks, target creature becomes marked until end of turn.

subrules.name: 702.228b
subrules.rule: Marked is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that spells and abilities can identify. Only permanents can be or become marked.

subrules.name: 702.229a
subrules.rule: Coalesce appears on Revelation cards. It represents three static abilities: one that functions while the card is in a player's graveyard and two that function while the card is on the stack. “Coalesce (cost)” means “You may cast this card from your graveyard by paying (cost) rather than paying its mana cost” and “If the coalesce cost was paid, put this card onto the battlefield as a Horror creature. If this spell is a kindred, it also has each of this spell's creature types. If it would leave the battlefield, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else,” and “If the coalesce cost was paid, exile this card instead of putting it anywhere else anytime it would leave the stack except being put onto the battlefield with its coalesce ability.”

subrules.name: 702.229b
subrules.rule: A copy of a spell cast for its coalesce cost is unable to enter the battlefield, as a token or otherwise. The spell effect of the copy will still happen as normal.

subrules.name: 702.230a
subrules.rule: Chosen one is an activated ability of some permanents. “Chosen one” means “(W)(U)(B)(R)(G): Transform this permanent.”

El, Humble Apprentice//Velir, End of All Worlds

subrules.name: 702.231a
subrules.rule: Desecrate is a triggered ability. “Desecrate” means “When this creature enters, you may sacrifice an artifact or land.”

subrules.name: 702.231b
subrules.rule: A creature with desecrate “desecrates a permanent” when the controller of the desecrate ability sacrifices a permanent as that ability resolves.

subrules.name: 702.232a
subrules.rule: Bloodprice is a static ability that functions while the spell with bloodprice is on the stack. “Bloodprice (cost)” means “You may cast this spell by paying (cost) and sacrificing a creature rather than paying its mana cost.

subrules.name: 702.233a
subrules.rule: Defiance is a triggered ability of some creatures. “Defiance” means “Whenever this creature is dealt damage, if it isn't defiant, put a +1/+1 counter on it and it becomes defiant.”

subrules.name: 702.234a
subrules.rule: Enspirit represents two static abilities, one that functions while the spell with enspirit is on the stack and another that functions both while it's on the stack and while it's on the battlefield. “Enspirit” means “As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may exile a nonenchantment creature you control until this spell is put from the stack into a zone other than the battlefield or the permanent this spell becomes leaves the battlefield” and “If you chose to pay this spell's additional cost, its total cost is reduced by an amount of generic mana equal to the exiled card's mana value.” Paying a spell's enspirit cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.234b
subrules.rule: The two abilities represented by enspirit are linked. The first ability may also be linked with any number of other abilities printed on the card with enspirit which refer either to “the exiled card” or to cards “exiled with [this object]”. See rule 607, “Linked Abilities.”

subrules.name: 702.234c
subrules.rule: You choose which creature to exile as you choose to pay a spell's enspirit cost (see rule 601.2b), and you exile that creature as you pay the total cost (see rule 601.2h).

subrules.name: 702.234d
subrules.rule: A creature “becomes enspirited” when it's exiled to pay a spell's enspirit cost. Abilities that trigger when a creature becomes enspirited are leaves-the-battlefield abilities (see rule 603.6c).

subrules.name: 702.235a
subrules.rule: A harmony ability is a special kind of triggered ability that does not have a built-in trigger condition. Instead, it may be triggered by the harmonize action. (see rule 701.81).

subrules.name: 702.236a
subrules.rule: Tithe is an ability of some cards. It behaves differently on permanent and nonpermanent cards.

subrules.name: 702.236b
subrules.rule: On a permanent card, tithe is a triggered ability. “Tithe” on a permanent means “When this permanent enters, you may tap three other untapped artifacts and/or creatures you control.” Tapping the three permanents is a cost (see rule 118) and may be referred to as paying the permanent's tithe.

subrules.name: 702.236c
subrules.rule: On an instant or sorcery card, tithe is a static ability that functions while the spell with tithe is on the stack. “Tithe” on an instant or sorcery spell means “As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may tap three untapped artifacts and/or creatures you control.” Paying an instant or sorcery spell's tithe cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h. An instant or sorcery spell's tithe cost may also simply be referred to as its tithe.

subrules.name: 702.237a
subrules.rule: Eureka! is a triggered ability of some permanents. “Eureka!” means “At the beginning of each end step, you get a research counter if you cast a spell this turn. Then if you have eight or more research couters, you lose all research counters, then create your choice of Cultivating Spheres, Mirror of Possibilities, and Thrice-Folded Lotus.”

subrules.name: 702.237b
subrules.rule: Cultivating Spheres is a colorless Masterpiece artifact token with “At the beginning of your draw step, draw an additional card” and “You may play an additional land on each of your turns.”

subrules.name: 702.237c
subrules.rule: Mirror of Possibilities is a colorless Masterpiece artifact token with “Whenever you cast a spell, you may pay {3}. If you do, copy it. You may choose new targets for the copy”

subrules.name: 702.237d
subrules.rule: Thrice-Folded Lotus is a colorless Masterpiece artifact token with “{T}: Add three mana of any one color” and “{3}, {T}: Thrice-Folded Lotus deals 3 damage to any target.”

subrules.name: 702.237e
subrules.rule: Eureka! checks if you cast a spell this turn when the ability resolves. This means you can cast a spell in response to the trigger to get a counter.

subrules.name: 702.238a
subrules.rule: Memento appears on some double-faced cards. It represents three static abilities: one that functions while the card with memento is in a player's graveyard and two that function while the spell with memento is on the stack. “Memento (cost)” means “You may cast this card from your graveyard by paying (cost) rather than paying its mana cost,” “If this memento cost was paid, put this card onto the battlefield transformed. If it would leave the battlefield, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else,” and “If the memento cost was paid, exile this card instead of putting it anywhere else anytime it would leave the stack except being put onto the battlefield with its memento ability.”

matched_card_names: Descend on the Helpless//Cormoran, Raven Monarch
Shatter the Mask//Jirada, Elder of Caulte

subrules.name: 702.239a
subrules.rule: Leitmotif appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents a static ability that functions while the spell is on the stack and may create a delayed triggered ability. “Leitmotif” means “If this spell was cast from your hand, instead of putting it into your graveyard as it resolves, exile it and, when you cast a spell that shares a color with this card, you may cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.239b
subrules.rule: Casting a spell as an effect of its leitmotif ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.239c
subrules.rule: Multiple instances of leitmotif on the same spell are redundant.

subrules.name: 702.239d
subrules.rule: Type leitmotif is a variant of the leitmotif ability. “Type leitmotif” means “If this spell was cast from your hand, instead of putting it into your graveyard as it resolves, exile it and, when you cast a spell that shares a type with this card, you may cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.240a
subrules.rule: Embellish represents a static ability that functions while the card with embellish is on the stack and a triggered ability that functions on the battlefield, and one which may create a delayed triggered ability. “Embellish (cost)” means “You may cast this card as by paying (cost) rather than its mana cost,” and “When this permanent enters, if its embellish cost was paid, create a 1/1 blue Thopter artifact creature token with flying.” Casting a spell for its embellish cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.241a
subrules.rule: Encourage is an activated ability. “Encourage” means “{T}: Another target creature you control gets +1/+1 until end of turn. Activate this ability only any time you could cast a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.241b
subrules.rule: A creature with encourage “encourages a creature” and that creature “becomes encouraged” as the encourage ability resolves.

subrules.name: 702.242a
subrules.rule: Tether appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two abilities. The first is a spell ability that functions while the spell with tether is on the stack. The second is a static ability that functions while the card with tether is in the exile zone. “Tether” means “If this spell is represented by a card, you may exile this card tethered to a creature you control” and “When the creature this card is tethered to dies, you may cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.242b
subrules.rule: The term “tethered” describes the relationship between the card with tether while in the exile zone and the creature chosen when the spell represented by that card resolves.

subrules.name: 702.242c
subrules.rule: The card with tether remains tethered to the chosen creature as long as the card with tether remains exiled and the creature remains on the battlefield. The card remains tethered to that object even if it changes controller or stops being a creature, as long as it remains on the battlefield.

subrules.name: 702.242d
subrules.rule: If the permanent is put into a graveyard while not a creature, the 'dies' trigger of tether will still trigger.

subrules.name: 702.242e
subrules.rule: Tether to type is a variant of the tether ability. “Tether to [type]” means “If this spell is represented by a card, you may exile this card tethered to a [type] you control” and “When the permanent this card is tethered to is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, you may cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.243a
subrules.rule: Assault is a triggered ability of some creatures. “Assault (cost)” means “Whenever this creatures attacks, if it has no +1/+1 counters on it, you may pay (cost). If you do, put a +1/+1 counter on it.”

subrules.name: 702.243b
subrules.rule: A creature “assaults” whenever its assault cost is paid.

subrules.name: 702.244a
subrules.rule: Gestalt represents two triggered abilities. “Gestalt” means “When this creature enters, you may merge it with a another creature you control. It becomes a gestalt permanent. Move any counters from this creature to the gestalt permanent and attach any cards attached to this creature to the gestalt permanent.” and “When another creature you control enters, you may merge it with this permanent. It becomes a gestalt permanent. Move any counters from that creature to the gestalt permanent and attach any cards attached to that creature to the gestalt permanent.”

subrules.name: 702.244b
subrules.rule: A gestalt permanent has all abilities of each card and token that represents it. Its other characteristics are derived from the topmost card or token.

subrules.name: 702.245a
subrules.rule: “Harness” means “As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may tap an untapped creature you control. This spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is that creature's power.”

subrules.name: 702.245b
subrules.rule: The creature tapped this way “harnesses” that spell.

subrules.name: 702.246a
subrules.rule: Pressure is a static ability that functions while the spell with pressure is on the stack. “Pressure (cost)” means “You may pay (cost) rather than pay this spell’s mana cost as you cast this spell if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard.”

subrules.name: 702.246b
subrules.rule: The final cost of a spell is locked in before costs are paid, meaning a spell can be cast for its pressure cost while also having an additional cost that exiles cards from its controller's graveyard that would result in having fewer than seven cards in it.

subrules.name: 702.247a
subrules.rule: Slipstream is an evasion ability. A creature with slipstream can't be blocked as long as each attacking creature has slipstream.

subrules.name: 702.247b
subrules.rule: If creatures with and without slipstream are attacking and then each attacking creature without slipstream is removed from combat, creatures with slipstream can't be blocked. However, if blockers have already been declared, those creatures will still be blocked.

subrules.name: 702.248a
subrules.rule: Beckon is an activated ability of Deity permanents. “Beckon (type)—(cost)” means “(Cost): If this permanent isn't a creature, it becomes a (type) creature in addition to its other types.”

subrules.name: 702.248b
subrules.rule: A beckon effect lasts indefinitely.

subrules.name: 702.248c
subrules.rule: If a Deity somehow becomes a noncreature again, its beckon ability can be reactivated.

subrules.name: 702.248d
subrules.rule: If a Deity is a creature, its beckon ability will have no affect, even if it's not the creature type it would become.

subrules.name: 702.249a
subrules.rule: Mimic is an activated ability. “Mimic (cost)” means “(Cost): Choose a number. Activate only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.249b
subrules.rule: Any number can be chosen. If the permanent does not have a shape associated with that number, it will only have its base characteristics.

subrules.name: 702.249c
subrules.rule: Abilities of a permanent with mimic that trigger when it "takes this shape" trigger after its mimic ability resolves, if it has that ability. These will trigger even if the creature did not change into this shape from another one.

subrules.name: 702.250a
subrules.rule: Glitch represents two static abilities that function while the spell with glitch is on the stack. “Glitch [cost]” means “You may pay an additional [cost] any number of times as you cast this spell” and “For each time you chose to pay this spell's glitch cost, change its text by removing one instance of text in [] brackets.” Paying a spell’s glitch cost(s) follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.250b
subrules.rule: If a spell’s controller declares the intention to pay any of that spell’s glitch costs, that spell is “glitched.”

subrules.name: 702.250c
subrules.rule: If a glitched spell is copied, the choice of which instances of bracketed text were removed will be copied as well.

subrules.name: 702.250d
subrules.rule: Persistent glitch is an activated ability and variant of the glitch ability found on permanents. “Persistent glitch [cost]” means “[Cost]: Change the text of this permanent by removing one instance of text in [] brackets.”

subrules.name: 702.251a
subrules.rule: Respawn is a triggered ability. “Respawn” means “When this creature dies, if it attacked this turn, return it to its owner's hand.”

subrules.name: 702.252a
subrules.rule: Align is a static ability that functions while the spell or ability with align is on the stack. “Align X” means “Choose up to X ⭐ worth of modes. You may choose the same mode more than once.” See rule 700.2i.

subrules.name: 702.253a
subrules.rule: Ascend is an activated ability. “Ascend (cost)” means “(cost): Exile this creature, then return it to the battlefield transformed. Activate only any time you could cast a sorcery.”

matched_card_names: Savants of the Ley//Tyrants of Bundan

subrules.name: 702.254a
subrules.rule: Acquiesce appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two abilities. The first is a spell ability that functions while the spell with acquiesce is on the stack. The second is a triggered ability that functions while the card with acquiesce is in the exile zone. “Acquiesce” means “If you cast this spell from your hand, exile it” and “Whenever one or more creatures you control deal combat damage to an opponent, you may cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.254b
subrules.rule: An exiled card with acquiesce does not need to be cast at the first opportunity. If it is not, the ability will still trigger the next time combat damage is dealt.

subrules.name: 702.255a
subrules.rule: Monument is an ability found on the front face of some transforming double-faced cards (see rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards”). “Monument [cost]” means “You may cast this card transformed from your graveyard by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost. If this spell would leave the stack other than being put onto the battlefield, or the permanent it becomes would leave the battlefield, exile it instead.” See rule 712.4b.

subrules.name: 702.255b
subrules.rule: A resolving transforming double-faced spell that was cast using its monument ability enters the battlefield with its back face up.
