subrules.name: 702.256a
subrules.rule: Successor is an activated ability that functions while the card with successor is in a graveyard. “Successor (cost)” means “(cost), Exile this card from your graveyard: Create a token that’s a copy of this card, except it has no mana cost and it has base power and toughness 1/1. Activate only any time you could cast a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.256b
subrules.rule: Successor will create a token that's a copy of the card as it was in the graveyard, rather than it is in exile.

subrules.name: 702.257a
subrules.rule: Infamy is a triggered ability. “Infamy N” means “When this creature deals combat damage to a player, if it isn’t infamous, put N +1/+1 counters on it and it becomes infamous.”

subrules.name: 702.257b
subrules.rule: Infamous is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that the infamy ability and other spells and abilities can identify. Only permanents can be or become infamous. Once a permanent becomes infamous, it stays infamous until it leaves the battlefield. Infamous is neither an ability nor part of the permanent’s copiable values.

subrules.name: 702.257c
subrules.rule: If a creature has multiple instances of infamy, each triggers separately. The first such ability to resolve will cause the creature to become infamous, and subsequent abilities will have no effect. (See rule 603.4)

subrules.name: 702.258a
subrules.rule: Overclock is a keyword that represents two triggered abilities. “Overclock” means “When this creature enters, if you control both this creature and another artifact, you may overclock another artifact you control for as long as both remain permanents on the battlefield under your control or until this creature overclocks another artifact” and “Whenever an artifact you control enters, if you control both that artifact and this creature, you may overclock this artifact for as long as both remain creatures on the battlefield under your control or until that creature overclocks another artifact.”

subrules.name: 702.258b
subrules.rule: An artifact becomes “overclocked” with another as the result of a overclock ability. Abilities may refer to an overclocked artifact, the artifact a creature overclocks, or whether an artifact is overclocked.

subrules.name: 702.258c
subrules.rule: A creature can only overclock one artifact, however an artifact may be overclocked by multiple creatures.

subrules.name: 702.258d
subrules.rule: An overclocked artifact stops being overclocked if any of the following occur: another player gains control of it or the creature overclocking it; it or the creature overclocking it leaves the battlefield; or the creature overclocking it overclocks another artifact.

subrules.name: 702.259a
subrules.rule: Simulacrum is a triggered ability. “Simulacrum” means “When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, exile it from your graveyard. If you do, create a token that's a copy of this card, except it's colorless, it's 1/1, it has no mana cost, and it's a Crystal artifact in addition to its other types.”

subrules.name: 702.259b
subrules.rule: If a permanent with simulacrum is controlled by a player other than its owner when it dies, that player will be unable to exile it from their graveyard, and won't create the token copy.

subrules.name: 702.260a
subrules.rule: Improve is an activated ability of some permanents. “Impove [cost]” means “[cost]: Put a +1/+1 counter on this permanent. This ability costs (1) more to activate for each +1/+1 counter on this permanent. Improve only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.261a
subrules.rule: Ride is an activated ability of some double-faced cards. “Ride [cost]” means “[cost]: Transform this creature and attach it to target creature you control that doesn't have a Steed enchantment attached to it. As long as this card remains attached to a permanent, you may pay [cost] any time you could cast a sorcery to unattach it from that permanent. Ride only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.261b
subrules.rule: If a Steed is on the battlefield not attached to a permanent, it transforms rather than being put into its owner's graveyard if able. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)

subrules.name: 702.261c
subrules.rule: The creature a Steed card enchants may be referred to as its “rider”. Effects that refer to a Steed's rider are identical to those that would refer to enchanted creature.

subrules.name: 702.261d
subrules.rule: One card (Bonescourge Kazadrak) allows its ride ability to be activated from its owner's graveyard. If this is done, the card will be put onto the battlefield transformed rather than transforming the card.

subrules.name: 702.261e
subrules.rule: One card (The Scourgebone Pact) states that its rider "can't dismount". This means a player can't pay [cost] to unattach the Steed from the creature it is attached to. The Steed will still transform back to its front face if it is unattached somehow, such as its rider leaving the battlefield.

matched_card_names: Scavenger of the Old Bay//Bay-Bandit's Snapper

subrules.name: 702.262a
subrules.rule: Agonize appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two static abilities: one that functions while the card is in a player’s graveyard and another that functions while the card is on the stack. “Agonize” means “You may cast this card from your graveyard if the resulting spell is an instant or sorcery spell by putting a -1/-1 counter on a creature you control as an additional cost to cast it” and “If this spell was cast using its agonize ability, exile this card instead of putting it anywhere else any time it would leave the stack.” Casting a spell using its agonize ability follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.263a
subrules.rule: Unveil is an activated ability of some permanents. “Unveil [cost]” means “[cost]: Transform this permanent. Activate only as a sorcery.” Transforming a permanent this way causes its controller to “unveil” it.

subrules.name: 702.264a
subrules.rule: Advance is a keyword ability that represents a static ability that functions while the spell with advance is on the stack, and an activated ability. “Advance [cost]” means “You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If you do, as the permanent it becomes enters the battlefield, it advances” and “[cost]: This permanent advances. Activate only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.264b
subrules.rule: “Advances” is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that other spells and abilities can identify. The number of times a permanent has advanced is not part of the permanent's copiable values.

subrules.name: 702.264c
subrules.rule: If a triggered ability refers to the mana that was spent to advance a permanent, it means the mana used to cast that spell if that ability was triggered by the creature advancing as a result of being cast for its advance ability, the mana used to activate its advance ability if that ability was triggered by the creature advancing as a result of its advanced activated ability resolving, and nothing if it is triggered in some other manner.

subrules.name: 702.265a
subrules.rule: Codex is a static ability of some permanents. “Codex — [list of card names]” means “As this permanent enters, conjure cards named [list of card names] and shuffle them into an additional, face up, library.”

subrules.name: 702.265b
subrules.rule: The additional library is referred to as “the codex's library” by the permanent with the codex ability that created it.

subrules.name: 702.265c
subrules.rule: “This codex's contents” refers to any card that shares a name with a name in the permanent's codex ability, regardless of if that card was conjured by the specific codex.

subrules.name: 702.265d
subrules.rule: If a card would be put into the codex's library, that card is put in that library face up.

subrules.name: 702.265e
subrules.rule: If a permanent with codex leaves the battlefield, the archived library remains, but is no longer affected by any effects the permanent provided.

subrules.name: 702.265f
subrules.rule: Cards are not revealed when they are put into a face up library. Cards can still become revealed even though the cards are already visible.

subrules.name: 702.265g
subrules.rule: If another player gains control of a permanent with codex, they will control any effects of the permanent, but will not own the codex's library. This means cards from the codex's library can't go into that player's hand, graveyard, or library, and cards that player owns can't be put into the codex's library. Effects of the codex may still allow them to manipulate or play the cards in that library.

subrules.name: 702.266a
subrules.rule: A death knell ability is a special kind of triggered ability that does not have a built-in trigger condition. Instead, it may be triggered by spells, abilities, or game rules (see 702.266b)

subrules.name: 702.266b
subrules.rule: As a creature dies, its controller may choose a death knell ability of that creature or another permanent they control. Choosing an ability this way causes it to trigger.

subrules.name: 702.267a
subrules.rule: Golden age on an instant or sorcery spell represents a spell ability. It means “If you've cast an instant or sorcery spell this turn, activated a nonmana ability this turn, and attacked this turn, and you're not in a renaissance, you're in a renaissance for the rest of the game.”

subrules.name: 702.267b
subrules.rule: Golden age on a permanent represents a static ability. It means “Any time you've cast an instant or sorcery spell this turn, activated a nonmana ability this turn, and attacked this turn, and you're not in a renaissance, you're in a renaissance for the rest of the game”

subrules.name: 702.267c
subrules.rule: Being in a renaissance is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that other rules and effects can identify. Any number of players may be in a renaissance at the same time.

subrules.name: 702.267d
subrules.rule: After a player enters a renaissance, continuous effects are reapplied before the game checks to see if the game state or preceding events have matched any trigger conditions.

subrules.name: 702.268a
subrules.rule: Showcase appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two abilities: a static ability that functions while the spell with showcase is on the stack and a spell ability. “Showcase [cost]” means “You may pay [cost] rather than pay this spell’s mana cost as you cast this spell” and “If this spell’s showcase cost was paid, exile this card, then create a 1/1 red Bard creature token with “This creature can't block.” Whenever that token attacks, you may copy the exiled card and cast it without paying its mana cost.” Casting a spell using its showcase ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

matched_card_names: For the Court of the Queen

subrules.name: 702.269a
subrules.rule: Rerun appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents a static ability that functions while the spell is on the stack and may create a delayed triggered ability. “Rerun” means “If this spell was cast from your hand, instead of putting it into your graveyard as it resolves, exile it and, whenever a creature you control dies, you may cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.269b
subrules.rule: Casting a spell as an effect of its rerun ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.269c
subrules.rule: Multiple instances of rerun on the same spell are redundant.

subrules.name: 702.270a
subrules.rule: Reprocess represents a static ability that functions while the card with reprocess is in a player’s graveyard. “Reprocess (cost)” means “You may copy this card, then cast the copy from your graveyard by paying (cost) and exiling this card from your graveyard rather than paying its mana cost. Each mana spent to pay (cost) must be produced by a source with a unique name.” Casting a spell using its reprocess ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.270b
subrules.rule: Any amount of mana from sources without a name may be spent on reprocess costs.

subrules.name: 702.271a
subrules.rule: Wander appears on some permanent cards. “Wander (cost)” means “You may cast this permanent from the battlefield for (cost).” Casting a spell using its wander ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.272a
subrules.rule: Legacy is an ability found on the back face of some modal double-faced cards (see rule 712, “Double-Faced Cards”). “Legacy” means “You may cast this spell from your graveyard, but not from anywhere else,” “If this spell would leave the stack other than being put onto the battlefield, exile it instead,” and “If this permanent would leave the battlefield, exile it instead.” See rule 712.4b.

subrules.name: 702.273a
subrules.rule: Reconstruct represents three static abilities, one that functions while the card with reconstruct is in a graveyard, and two that functions while the spell with reconstruct is on the stack. “Reconstruct [cost]” means “You may cast this spell from your graveyard by paying [cost] and sacrificing a permanent rather than paying its mana cost,” “If you chose to pay this spell’s reconstruct cost, its total cost is reduced by an amount of generic mana equal to the sacrificed permanent’s mana value,” and “If the reconstruct cost was paid, exile this card instead of putting it anywhere else any time it would leave the stack.” Casting a spell using its reconstruct ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

Life as a Means to a Triumph

subrules.name: 702.274a
subrules.rule: Rhapsody is a keyword ability that represents two static abilities, one that functions while the spell with rhapsody is on the stack, and another that functions while the permanent with rhapsody is on the battlefield. “Rhapsody [cost]” means “You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If you do, it has base power and toughness 4/4” and “Any time you could cast a sorcery, you may pay [cost]. If you do, this permanent has base power and toughness 4/4.”

subrules.name: 702.274b
subrules.rule: The second ability of rhapsody is a special action, and can only be modified by abilities that explicitly modify the rhapsody action.

subrules.name: 702.275a
subrules.rule: Chronicle is a static ability found on chronicle cards. “Chronicle” means “As this permanent enters the battlefield, put a lore counter on it,” and “As your precombat main phase begins, put a lore counter on this permanent unless it has a number of lore counters greater than or equal to its final chapter number.” The latter is a turn-based action and does not use the stack.

subrules.name: 702.276a
subrules.rule: Colossal is a keyword ability that represents a static ability that functions while the spell with colossal is on the stack, and an activated ability. “Colossal N—[cost]” means “You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If you do, the permanent it becomes enters the battlefield with N +1/+1 counters on it” and “[cost]: If this permanent has no +1/+1 counters on it, put N +1/+1 counters on it. Activate only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.277a
subrules.rule: Compose appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents a static ability that functions while the spell is on the stack and may create a delayed triggered ability. “Compose” means “If this spell was cast from your hand, instead of putting it into your graveyard as it resolves, exile it and create a colorless Saga enchantment token with “{r3}—Copy the exiled card. You may cast the copy without paying its mana cost.”

subrules.name: 702.277b
subrules.rule: The card with compose will only be copied if the same object remains in exile by the time its associated Saga tokens have their final chapter ability trigger.

subrules.name: 702.277c
subrules.rule: Casting a spell as an effect of its Saga's ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.277d
subrules.rule: Multiple instances of compose will cause multiple Saga tokens to be created, each of which will be able to copy the original card with compose.

subrules.name: 702.278a
subrules.rule: Arise is an activated ability that functions while the card with revive is in a graveyard. “Arise (cost)” means “(cost), Exile this card from your graveyard: Create a token that’s a copy of this card, except it's black, it's a Zombie in addition to its other types, and it has 'This creature can't block.' Activate this ability only any time you could cast a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.278b
subrules.rule: Arise will create a token that's a copy of the card as it was in the graveyard, rather than it is in exile.

subrules.name: 702.279a
subrules.rule: Refine represents two static abilities that function while the spell with refine is on the stack. “Refine [cost]” means “You may cast this spell by paying [cost] and sacrificing an artifact rather than paying its mana cost” and “If you chose to pay this spell’s refine cost, its total cost is reduced by an amount of generic mana equal to the sacrificed artifact’s mana value.” Casting a spell using its refine ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.279b
subrules.rule: You choose which artifact to sacrifice as you choose to pay a spell’s refine cost (see rule 601.2b), and you sacrifice that artifact as you pay the total cost (see rule 601.2h).

subrules.name: 702.280a
subrules.rule: Resilience is a triggered ability. “Resilience” means “When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, exile it, then create a token that's a copy of it, except the token is 1/1 and doesn't have resilience.”

subrules.name: 702.280b
subrules.rule: If a permanent has multiple instances of resilience, multiple 1/1 token copies of it will be created, but those tokens will lose all instances of resilience.

subrules.name: 702.281a
subrules.rule: Breach is a triggered ability found on some creatures. “Breach” means “Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, you may have it become an Aura Curse enchantment with enchant opponent until your next turn. If you do, attach it to that player.”

subrules.name: 702.282a
subrules.rule: A recursive ability is a special kind of ability, written “Recursive — [Ability]”. Recursive abilities can be static, activated, triggered, or spell abilities. Recursive has no rules meaning other than to be a designation other effects can identify.

subrules.name: 702.282b
subrules.rule: A nonrecursive ability is any ability that is not recursive.

subrules.name: 702.283a
subrules.rule: Attain is an activated ability of some double-faced permanents. “Attain (cost)” means “(cost): Transform this permanent. Spend mana of at least three different colors to activate this ability. Activate only as a sorcery.”

subrules.name: 702.283b
subrules.rule: One card (Janneke, Adept of Mortals) says a player “may spend any number of colors of mana to activate attain abilities.” This causes the “Spend mana of at least three different colors to activate this ability.” part of attain abilities to be ignored.

subrules.name: 702.283c
subrules.rule: Attain will check the colors of mana actually spent to activate the ability, even if an effect allows them to be spent as though they were mana of a different color.

subrules.name: 702.283d
subrules.rule: Some triggered abilities trigger when a player “attains” an object with a specified characteristic. Such an ability triggers if the object is transformed as a result of its attain ability and has the specified characteristic immediately after it does so.

subrules.name: 702.284a
subrules.rule: Deploy is a static ability. “Deploy N” means “As this permanent enters, you may tap any number of other untapped creatures you control with total power N or more. If you do, this permanent is deployed.” Tapping the creatures is a cost (see rule 118) and may be referred to as paying the permanent's deploy cost.

subrules.name: 702.284b
subrules.rule: Deployed is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that spells and abilities can identify. Only permanents can be or become deployed. Once a permanent becomes deployed, it stays deployed until it leaves the battlefield. Deployed is neither an ability nor part of the permanent's copiable values.

subrules.name: 702.284c
subrules.rule: A permanent “enters deployed” as it enters the battlefield if its deploy cost was paid.

subrules.name: 702.285a
subrules.rule: Disgraced represents a static ability and a triggered ability. “Disgraced N” means “This permanent enters the battlefield with N -1/-1 counters on it” and “Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, remove all -1/-1 counters from it.”

subrules.name: 702.286a
subrules.rule: Fleeting represents two static abilities, one that functions while the card with fleeting is on the stack, and one which may create a delayed triggered ability. “Fleeting (cost)” means “You may cast this card by paying (cost) rather than its mana cost,” and “If this spell's fleeting cost was paid, sacrifice the permanent this spell becomes at the beginning of the next end step.” Casting a spell for its fleeting cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.287a
subrules.rule: Voracious is a static ability. “Voracious N” means “As this object enters the battlefield, you may sacrifice up to N creatures and/or artifacts. This permanent enters the battlefield with a +1/+1 counter on it for each permanent sacrificed this way.”

subrules.name: 702.288a
subrules.rule: Lionize is an activated ability. "Lionize (cost)" means "(cost), Exile this card from your hand: Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature. It also gains the non-lionize abilities of this creature printed below this one until end of turn. After the current turn has ended, you may cast this card from exile.” Cards with lionize may have one or more abilities printed after the lionize ability. (Some cards with backup also have abilities printed before the backup ability.)

subrules.name: 702.288b
subrules.rule: Only abilities printed on the object with lionize are granted by its lionize ability. Any abilities gained by a card are not granted by a lionize ability.

subrules.name: 702.288c
subrules.rule: The abilities that a lionize ability grants are determined as the ability is put on the stack. They won’t change if the card with lionize loses any abilities after the ability is put on the stack but before it resolves.

subrules.name: 702.289a
subrules.rule: Surpass is an activated ability of some double faced cards. "Surpass (cost)" means "(cost): Transform this permanent. This ability costs {1} less to cast for each counter on this permanent. Activate only as a sorcery."

matched_card_names: The Lost and Seeking//Ameret, Shining and Proud

subrules.name: 702.290a
subrules.rule: Crumble is a keyword that represents four abilities. “Crumble [cost]” means “You may cast this card by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost,” "This permanent enters with three time counters if its crumble cost was paid," “At the beginning of your upkeep, if this permanent has a time counter on it, remove a time counter from it,” and “When the last time counter is removed from this permanent, sacrifice it and draw a card.” Casting a spell for its crumble cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.290b
subrules.rule: If a permanent has multiple instances of crumble, each works separately.

subrules.name: 702.291a
subrules.rule: Foreshadow represents two static abilities: one that functions on the stack and other that functions on the battlefield. "Foreshadow [cost]" means "You may cast this card by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost" and "If this spell's foreshadow cost was paid, entering the battlefield causes its abilities to trigger as though it died."

subrules.name: 702.292a
subrules.rule: Memory appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two static abilities: one that functions while the card is in a player’s graveyard and another that functions while the card is on the stack. “Memory (cost)” means “You may cast this card from your graveyard if the resulting spell is an instant or sorcery spell by paying (cost) and discarding a card rather than pay its mana cost” and “If this spell was cast using its memory ability, exile this card instead of putting it anywhere else any time it would leave the stack.” Casting a spell using its memory ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.293a
subrules.rule: Resurface appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two static abilities: one that functions while the card is in a player’s graveyard and another that functions while the card is on the stack. “Resurface [number]” means “You may cast this card from your graveyard if the resulting spell is an instant or sorcery spell by tapping one or more creatures you control with total power [number] or greater as an additional cost to cast it” and “If this spell was cast using its resurface ability, exile this card instead of putting it anywhere else any time it would leave the stack.” Casting a spell using its resurface ability follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.294a
subrules.rule: Siphon is a static ability that functions while the spell with siphon is on the stack. “Siphon” means “For each generic mana in this spell’s total cost, you may put a -1/-1 counter on a creature you control with toughness 1 or greater and less damage marked on it than its total toughness rather than pay that mana.”

subrules.name: 702.294b
subrules.rule: Multiple instances of siphon on the same spell are redundant.

subrules.name: 702.295a
subrules.rule: Transcend is a static ability. Each card printed with transcend is known as a Transcend card. It has a nonstandard layout that includes two or more ability boxes that are themselves keyword abilities. See rule C745, "Transcend Cards".

matched_card_names: Dai Gui, Pillar of Sea and Sky
Shi Hou, the Sun King//Sun King's Shadow

subrules.name: 702.296a
subrules.rule: Derange is a static ability that functions while the spell with derange is on the stack. “Derange N” means “As you cast this spell, you may mill exactly N cards.”

subrules.name: 702.296b
subrules.rule: A player with fewer than N cards in their library won't be able to mill any cards.

subrules.name: 702.296c
subrules.rule: A copy of a spell with derange won't be able to mill cards, unless the effect specifically casts a copy.

subrules.name: 702.297a
subrules.rule: Diverge is a static ability. Each card printed with diverge is known as a Diverge card. It has a nonstandard layout that includes two ability boxes that are themselves keyword abilities. See rule C750, "Diverge Cards".

subrules.name: 702.297b
subrules.rule: An object's "diverge abilities" refer to diverge as well as that object's divergent paths.

subrules.name: 702.298a
subrules.rule: Forsake is a static ability that appears on forsake cards that have a secondary set of mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics. Any time a player could cast a sorcery, they may pay {2} and exile a card with forsake from their hand face down. That player may look at that card as long as it remains in exile. After the current turn has ended, they may cast that card from exile "forsaken." If they do, the alternative set of its mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics are used. See 751, “Prototype Cards.”

subrules.name: 702.298b
subrules.rule: Exiling a card using its forsake ability is a special action, which doesn’t use the stack. See rule 116, “Special Actions.”

subrules.name: 702.298c
subrules.rule: If a player owns multiple forsake cards in exile, they must ensure that those cards can be easily differentiated from each other and from any other face-down cards in exile which that player owns. This includes knowing the order in which those cards were put into exile.

subrules.name: 702.298d
subrules.rule: If a player leaves the game, all face-down forsake cards that player owns must be revealed to all players. At the end of each game, all face-down forsake cards must be revealed to all players.

subrules.name: 702.299a
subrules.rule: Living ritual is a triggered ability found on Implement cards. "Living ritual" means "When this Equipment enters, create a 1/0 red Devil creature token or Sulmina, the Final Age, a legendary 3/2 black Demon creature with flying, indestructible, and "When there aren’t exactly three different names among Implements you control, exile this token." Then attach this Equipment to that token.

subrules.name: 702.300a
subrules.rule: Multitude is a keyword that represents a static ability and a triggered ability that function while the spell with multitude is on the stack. “Multitude (cost)” means “You may choose to pay (cost) rather than this spell's mana cost,” and “When you cast this spell, if you paid its multitude cost, copy it. If the spell has any targets, you may choose new targets for the copy.”

subrules.name: 702.301a
subrules.rule: Figment is a triggered ability. "Figment N" means "At the beginning of combat on your turn, you may tap any number of other creatures you control with total power 3 or greater. If you do, create a token that's a copy of this permanent, except it has haste. Sacrifice the token at the beginning of the next end step.

subrules.name: 702.302a
subrules.rule: Retinue is a triggered ability, and a designation given to a group of permanents, which usually are tokens created by a retinue ability.

subrules.name: 702.302b
subrules.rule: "Retinue — [list of P/Ts]" means "When this permanent enters, for each listed P/T, create a red Army creature token with that P/T. Put each token created this way in this permanent's retinue." This list may include entries in the form "X [P/T]". In that case, X tokens are created instead of just one.

subrules.name: 702.302c
subrules.rule: As a player declares attacks, if a creature in a retinue or a creature with a retinue attacks, all creatures in that retinue also attack this combat if able. They may attack other players or permanents.

subrules.name: 702.302d
subrules.rule: As a player declares blocks, if a creature in a retinue or a creature with a retinue block, all creatures in that retinue also block this combat if able. They may block other creatures.

subrules.name: 702.302e
subrules.rule: A permanent can't have more than one retinue. If more permanents are added at a later time, they will be added to the previous retinue, and not a new one.

subrules.name: 702.302f
subrules.rule: A permanent can't be in more than one retinue. If it is put into one, it is removed from any retinue it was already in. If it is put into multiple simultaneously, its controller chooses one.

subrules.name: 702.302g
subrules.rule: If a permanent would be put into the retinue of a permanent that is itself in a retinue, they are instead put into the same retinue as that permanent.

subrules.name: 702.302h
subrules.rule: A retinue will continue to exist even if the permanent that it belongs to is no longer on the battlefield. Certain effects may also create a retinue that belongs to no permanent.

subrules.name: 702.302i
subrules.rule: A permanent can't be put into its own retinue.

subrules.name: 702.303a
subrules.rule: Husk is a triggered ability. “Husk” means “When this Equipment enters, create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token with decayed, then attach this Equipment to it.”

subrules.name: 702.304a
subrules.rule: Lucid appears on some modal instant and sorceries. It represents a static ability that functions while the spell is on the stack. "Lucid" means "If you cast this spell from your hand or from exile, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else as it resolves. As you cast a modal instant or sorcery spell while this card is exiled, you may choose one of this card's modes. If you do, change the text of that spell by adding the chosen mode into one of its bulleted lists and put this card into its owner's graveyard."

subrules.name: 702.304b
subrules.rule: If you're applying more than one card with lucid onto a spell, you will put them all into their owner's graveyard and choose the order in which the effects will happen. The new modes will always be added to the end of the list.

subrules.name: 702.304c
subrules.rule: The spell has the characteristics of the main spell, plus the rules text found in the chosen mode of the lucid card. This is a text-changing effect (see rule 612, “Text-Changing Effects”). The spell doesn’t gain any other characteristics (name, mana cost, color, supertypes, card types, subtypes, etc.) of the lucid cards. Text gained by the spell that refers to a card by name refers to the spell on the stack, not the card from which the text was copied.

subrules.name: 702.304d
subrules.rule: If a mode with an associated cost, such as those found on cards with spree, is added to another spell, this cost will still need to be paid regardless if the new spell has spree.

subrules.name: 702.304e
subrules.rule: If a mode without an associated cost is added to a card with spree, the player will be unable to pay its associated cost and unable to choose the mode.

subrules.name: 702.304f
subrules.rule: If a mode with star or pawprint symbols is added to a modal spell which does not use them to select modes, the mode may be chosen regardless of those symbols.

subrules.name: 702.304g
subrules.rule: If a mode without stars or pawprints is added to a modal spell that does use them to select modes, the mode is not a legal choice.

subrules.name: 702.305a
subrules.rule: Practiced is a static ability that functions while the spell with practiced is on the stack. "Practiced" means "This spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is the number of creatures you've attacked with this turn."

subrules.name: 702.305b
subrules.rule: Practiced discounts the spell for each individual permanent you have declared an attack with this turn. That permanent does not need to be under your control or on the battlefield anymore. If it attacked multiple times in a turn, it is only counted once.

subrules.name: 702.306a
subrules.rule: Premonition is a static ability that functions while the card with premonition is in a player's hand. "Premonition (cost)" means "Any time you could cast a sorcery, you may pay (cost) and exile this card from your hand. If you do, create a token that's a copy of it. It enters with an additional decayed counter on it. After the current turn has ended, you may cast this card from exile."

subrules.name: 702.306b
subrules.rule: Exiling a card using its premonition ability is a special action, which doesn't use the stack. See rule 116, “Special Actions.”

subrules.name: 702.307a
subrules.rule: Stardom is a keyword ability that represents two static abilities, one that functions while the spell with stardom is on the stack, and another that functions while the permanent with stardom is on the battlefield. “Stardom [cost]” means “You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If you do, it has base power and toughness 4/4 and is legendary” and “Any time you have priority and this creature is attacking, you may pay [cost]. If you do, this permanent has base power and toughness 4/4 and is legendary. Take this action only once.”

subrules.name: 702.307b
subrules.rule: The second ability of stardom is a special action, and its cost can only be modified by abilities that explicitly modify the stardom action.

subrules.name: 702.308a
subrules.rule: Malign is a static ability. “Malign N” means “If you've attacked this turn, this permanent enters with N +1/+1 counters on it.”

subrules.name: 702.308b
subrules.rule: If an object has multiple instances of malign, each applies separately.
Some cards, such as those with archive and codex abilities, create additional libraries. These libraries are separated from your starting library.
An additional library with no cards in it ceases to exist the next time state-based actions are checked.
If a player would draw a card while they have multiple libraries and the draw effect doesn't specify a library, that player chooses which library they own to draw from.

subrules.name: 740.3a
subrules.rule: If a player would draw multiple cards at once, the library each card is drawn from is chosen separately.

subrules.name: 740.3b
subrules.rule: A player can't attempt to draw from an additional library that has no cards in it.

If a cost or an effect other than a static ability would refer to a player's undefined library and that player has multiple libraries, that effect's controller chooses any library that player has upon resolution and the effect is applied to that library. If that effect has no controller, that player chooses the library instead.
Example: Enlightened Tutor will shuffle the same library that was searched, and put the found card on top of that same library.

subrules.name: 740.4a
subrules.rule:
Static abilities that refer to a player's undefined library apply to all of that player’s libraries instead.
Example: Portent of the Long Winter says “Play with the top card of your library revealed.” and “Spells cost {X} more to cast, where X is the mana value of the top card of your library.” You will play with the top cards of all your libraries revealed, and X will be the total mana value of cards on top of each of your libraries.

Each Discovery card has a striated text box containing a number of progress symbols. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.
A progress symbol is a keyword ability that represents a static or triggered ability referred to as a progress ability.

subrules.name: 741.2a
subrules.rule: A progress symbol includes a Roman numeral, indicated here as “{rN},” or a bottle symbol, indicated here as “{Discovery}.” The numeral I represents 1, II represents 2, III represents 3, and so on.

subrules.name: 741.2b
subrules.rule: “{rN}—[Effect]” means “When one or more progress counters are put onto this Discovery, if the number of progress counters on it was less than N and became at least N, [effect].”

subrules.name: 741.2c
subrules.rule: “{rN1}, {rN2}—[Effect]” means the same as “{rN1}—[Effect]” and “{rN2}—[Effect].”

subrules.name: 741.2d
subrules.rule: “{Discovery}—[Abilities]” means “As long as this Discovery has a number of progress counters on it greater than or equal to its final progress number, it has '[abilities]'.”

subrules.name: 741.2e
subrules.rule: A Discovery’s final progress number is the greatest value among progress abilities it has plus 1. If a Discovery somehow has no progress abilities, its final progress number is 1.
Discoveries use progress counters to track their progress.

subrules.name: 741.3a
subrules.rule: As a Discovery enters the battlefield, its controller puts a progress counter on it.

subrules.name: 741.3b
subrules.rule: As a player’s precombat main phase begins, that player puts a progress counter on each Discovery they control. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack.

Each Mystery card is a double-faced card. The front face has a striated textbox containing a number of mystery symbols. Its illustration is  vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its typeline is along the bottom of the card. The back face is a standard Magic card.
A mystery symbol is a keyword ability that represents a static ability.

subrules.name: 742.2a
subrules.rule: A mystery symbol includes a magnifying glass symbol, indicated here as {mg}.

subrules.name: 742.2b
subrules.rule: {mg}—[Condition] means As [condition], decode this ability.

subrules.name: 742.2c
subrules.rule: Decode has no rules meaning, and is just a designation that the ability's condition has been met.
If a mystery card has one or more mystery abilities and each of those abilities is decoded, it transforms. This state-based action doesn't use the stack.

matched_card_names: Mystery of the Crashed Craft//Epsilon, Crash Captain
Mystery of the Dying Herds//Eta, Experimental Doctor

subrules.rule: Each Realm card has a striated textbox containing a number of realm abilities and a favor symbol. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its typeline is along the bottom of the card.
A realm ability is an activated ability printed on a Realm card that isn't part of a favor symbol.

subrules.name: 743.2a
subrules.rule: A realm ability can be activated only once. This is true even if the permanent with the realm ability is not a Realm.
A favor symbol is a keyword ability that represents a static ability,  which gives the Realm another ability referred to as a favor ability.

subrules.name: 743.3a
subrules.rule: A favor symbol includes a laurels symbol, indicated here as {fL}.

subrules.name: 743.3b
subrules.rule: {fL}—[Ability] means As long as you have activated each of this permanent's realm abilities, it has [ability].

subrules.name: 743.3c
subrules.rule: If a permanent somehow has a favor symbol but no realm abilities, it will have the favor ability.
Each Quest card has a striated text box containing a number of quest symbols. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.
An quest symbol is a keyword ability that represents a triggered ability referred to as an quest ability.

subrules.name: 744.2a
subrules.rule: An quest symbol includes a number, indicated here as “{N}.”

subrules.name: 744.2b
subrules.rule: “{N}—[Effect]” means “When one or more quest counters are put onto this Quest, if the number of quest counters on it was less than N and became at least N, [effect].”

subrules.name: 744.2c
subrules.rule: “{N1}, {N2}—[Effect]” means the same as “{N1}—[Effect]” and “{N2}—[Effect].”

subrules.name: 744.2d
subrules.rule: An Quest’s final quest number is the greatest value among quest abilities. If an Quest somehow has no quest abilities, its final quest number is 0.
Quests use quest counters to track their progress.

subrules.name: 744.3a
subrules.rule: As an Quest enters the battlefield, its controller puts a quest counter on it.

subrules.name: 744.3b
subrules.rule: Each Quest has a triggered ability that “adds a quest counter.” To add a quest counter, put a quest counter on the Quest that is the source of that triggered ability.

If the number of quest counters on an Quest permanent is greater than or equal to its final quest number, and it isn't the source of a quest ability that has triggered but not yet left the stack, that Quest's controller sacrifices it. This state-based action doesn't use the stack.

matched_card_names: A Slave's Vengeance//Crown of the Urchin King

subrules.rule: Each Transcend card has a striated text box containing two transcend level bars. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the left side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.

A transcend ability bar is a keyword ability that represents an activated ability. A transcend ability bar includes the activation cost of its activated ability and a subtype. Any abilities printed within the same text box section as the transcend ability bar are part of its activated ability.

subrules.name: 745.2a
subrules.rule: “[Cost]: [Subtype] — [Effect]” printed on a Transcend card means “[Cost]: This permanent becomes a [Subtype] in addition to its other types. Put a +1/+1 counter on it. [Effect]. Activate this ability only once, only as a sorcery, and only if each of its previous transcend abilities have been activated.”

subrules.name: 745.2b
subrules.rule: The phrase “previous transcend abilities” refers to each ability printed on the Transcend card above the ability being activated. It is possible for an object to gain multiple groups of transcend abilities, these abilities from other cards are not counted as previous transcend abilities, even if they happen to come from cards with the same name.

Any ability printed on a Transcend card that isn’t preceded by a transcend ability bar is treated normally. In particular, the Transcend card has the ability printed in its top text box section at all times. That ability may affect the game if it’s a static ability, it may trigger if it’s a triggered ability, and it can be activated if it’s an activated ability.

matched_card_names: Dai Gui, Pillar of Sea and Sky
Shi Hou, the Sun King//Sun King's Shadow

subrules.rule: Wu Xing cards have a unique copiable characteristic called their “wu xing number”. As a Wu Xing card is cast or a spell becomes a Wu Xing card, its wu xing number becomes equal to the number of colors of mana spent to cast it.

Wu Xing cards contain a colors table. The colors table appears as a chart with multiple striations. Each striation includes a number and an effect associated with that number. Each striation of the colors chart means “If this spell's wu xing number is at least [number], [effect].” While casting and resolving a Wu Xing card, use the color table to determine what happens.
Each Gallery card has a striated text box containing two gallery level bars. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the left side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.

A gallery level bar is a keyword ability that represents both an activated ability and a static ability. A gallery level bar includes the activation cost of its activated ability and a flavor word. Any abilities printed within the same text box section as the gallery level bar are part of its static ability.

subrules.name: 747.2a
subrules.rule: “[Cost]: [Flavor word] — [Abilities]” means “[Cost]: Unlock the work [Flavor word]. Activate only if none of this Gallery's works have been unlocked and only as a sorcery” and “As long as this Gallery has unlocked [Flavor word], it has [abilities].”

subrules.name: 747.2b
subrules.rule: An unlocked work is a designation that any permanent can have. A Gallery retains its unlocked works even if it stops being a Gallery. Unlocked works are not a copiable characteristic.

Any ability printed on a Gallery card that isn’t preceded by a gallery level bar is treated normally. In particular, the Gallery has the ability printed in its top text box section at all times. That ability may affect the game if it’s a static ability, it may trigger if it’s a triggered ability, and it can be activated if it’s an activated ability.
Each chronicle card has a striated text box and contains two chronicle symbols.

A chapter symbol is a keyword ability that represents a static ability. The chapter symbol includes either a single number, indicated here as “rN,” or a range of numbers, indicated here as “rN2-rN3.” Any abilities printed within the same text box striation as a level symbol are part of its static ability.

subrules.name: 748.2a
subrules.rule: “{LORE rN} [Effect]” means “When one or more lore counters are put onto this permanent, if the number of lore counters on it was less than N and became at least N, [effect].”

subrules.name: 748.2b
subrules.rule: “{LORE rN2-rN3} [Effect]” means the same as “{LORE rN2} [Effect]” and “{LORE rN3} [Effect]” for each number in the range.

subrules.name: 748.2c
subrules.rule: A chronicle card’s final chapter number is the greatest value among chapter abilities it has. If a chronicle card somehow has no chapter abilities, its final chapter number is 0.
The text box striations have no game significance other than clearly demarcating which effects are associated with which chapter symbol. Chronicle cards each contain only one text box.
Any ability a chronicle card has that isn’t preceded by a chapter symbol is treated normally. In particular, each chronicle permanent has its chronicle ability (see rule 702.274) at all times.
Some enchantments have the subtype Saga and associated chapter abilities. Lore counters from either source will interact with both forms of chapter abilities. See rule 714, “Saga Cards.”
Each Module card has a striated text box containing three submodule bars. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the left side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.

A submodule is a keyword ability that represents an activated ability. A submodule bar includes the activation cost of its activated ability and a flavor word. Any abilities printed within the same text box section as the submodule bar are part of its activated ability.

subrules.name: 749.2a
subrules.rule: “[Cost]: [Flavor word] — [Effect]” means “[Cost]: [Effect]. Activate this ability only once. Activate this ability only as a sorcery or if a spell or ability instructs you to activate a submodule.”
A Module card has the intrinsic ability “When this permanent enters the battlefield, you may activate one of its submodules without paying its activation cost.”
Each Diverge cards has a striated text box containing two divergent paths. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the left side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.

A divergent ability is a keyword ability that represents an activated ability. A divergent path includes the activation cost of its activated ability and a subtype. Any abilities printed within the same text box section as the divergent path are part of its activated ability.

subrules.name: 750.2a
subrules.rule: "[Cost]: [Subtype] — [Effect]" printed on a Diverge card means "[Cost]: This permanent becomes a [Subtype] in addition to its other types. Put a +1/+1 counter on it. [Effect]. Activate this ability only as a sorcery, and only if none of its divergent paths have been activated."

subrules.name: 750.2b
subrules.rule: One card (Quarry of the Ivory Mask) allows players to activate diverge abilities any time they could cast an instant. This effect allows players to ignore the timing restriction associated with divergent paths. Players will still be unable to activate an object's divergent paths in response to its first activation, even if that ability hasn't resolved yet.

subrules.name: 750.2c
subrules.rule: It is possible for an object to gain multiple pairs of divergent paths. If the permanent has activated any divergent paths, including any it may no longer have, it will still be unable to activate paths from these alternate groups.

Any ability printed on a Diverge card that isn't preceded by a divergent path is treated normally. In particular, the Diverge card has the abilities printed in its top text box sections at all times. That ability may affect the game if it’s a static ability, it may trigger if it’s a triggered ability, and it can be activated if it’s an activated ability.

Forsake cards have a two-part frame, with a smaller frame inset below the type line of the card. The inset frame contains the forsake keyword ability as well as a second set of mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics.

The mana cost, power, and toughness in the inset frame represent alternative characteristics that the object may have while it is a spell or while it is a permanent on the battlefield. The card’s normal characteristics appear as usual.

subrules.name: 751.2a
subrules.rule: The existence and values of these alternative characteristics are part of the object’s copiable values.

Under most circumstances, a player can only cast a forsake card normally. If the card was exiled with its forsake ability, the player who did so will be able to cast the spell "forsaken" from exile, but not able to cast it normally this way (see rule 702.298, “Forsake”).

subrules.name: 751.3a
subrules.rule: While casting a forsaken spell, use only its alternative mana cost and/or power and toughness when evaluating those characteristics to see if it can be cast.

subrules.name: 751.3b
subrules.rule: Both a forsaken spell and the permanent it becomes have only its alternative set of mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics. If that mana cost includes one or more colored mana symbols, the spell and the permanent it becomes are also that color or colors (see rule 105.2).

subrules.name: 751.3c
subrules.rule: If a forsaken spell is copied, the copy is also a forsaken spell. It has the alternative mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics of the spell and not the normal mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics of the card that represents the forsaken spell. Any rule or effect that refers to a forsaken spell refers to the copy as well.

subrules.name: 751.3d
subrules.rule: If a permanent that was a forsaken spell is copied, the copy has the alternative mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics of the permanent and not the normal power and toughness characteristics of the card that represents that permanent. Any rule or effect that refers to a permanent that was a forsaken spell refers to the copy as well.
In every zone except the stack or the battlefield, and while on the stack or the battlefield when not cast as a forsaken spell, a forsake card has only its normal characteristics.
A forsake card’s characteristics other than its mana cost, power, and toughness, and color remain the same whether it was cast as a forsaken spell or cast normally.

A results table appears as a list or as a chart with multiple striations within a card's rules text. Each list item or striation includes possible results and an effect associated with those results. The possible results indicated could be a single number, a range of numbers with two endpoints in the form “N1–N2,” or a range with a single endpoint in the form “N+.” Each one means “If the result was in this range, [effect].”

An instruction to generate a result (such as rolling a die), any instructions to modify that result printed in the same paragraph, any additional instructions based on the result, and the associated results table are all part of one ability.

Some effects in results charts may instruct the player to do the result generating action again, such as “Roll again.” when rolling a die. This additional action will reuse the same conditions, including any applicable modifiers.
Tale cards have a two-part card frame, with a smaller frame inset within their text box.

The text that appears in the inset frame on the right defines alternative characteristics that the object may have while it’s a spell. The card’s normal characteristics appear as usual, although with a smaller text box on the left.

subrules.name: 753.2a
subrules.rule: The inset frame of a tale card is called a “Tale spell.” If a rule or effect refers to a card, spell, or permanent that has a Tale, it refers to an object for which these alternative characteristics exist, even if the object currently doesn’t use them.

subrules.name: 753.2b
subrules.rule: The existence and values of these alternative characteristics are part of the object’s copiable values.

subrules.name: 753.2c
subrules.rule: Although tale cards are printed with multiple sets of characteristics, each tale card is only one card. For example, a player who has drawn or discarded a tale card has drawn or discarded one card, not two.
Tale cards can’t be cast using the alternative characteristics found within their inset frames. Rather, these characteristics are used to define characteristics of copies which may be cast.

subrules.name: 753.3a
subrules.rule: As a permanent with a Tale enters or a permanent which has not cast its Tale gains a Tale, its controller creates a copy of the Tale in exile, except that copy has only the characteristics of that permanent’s Tale, ignoring other exceptions to the copying process that apply to that permanent. Those characteristics become the copy’s normal characteristics. This copy remains in exile for as long as the permanent remains on the battlefield, has the Tale, and has not cast its Tale. This is an exception to rule 704.5e. For as long as the copy remains in exile, the permanent’s controller may cast the copy. That permanent has "cast its Tale" at the time the spell becomes cast (see rule 601.2i).

subrules.name: 753.3b
subrules.rule: If a Tale spell is copied, the copy is also a Tale spell. Any rule or effect that refers to a spell cast as a Tale spell refers to the copy as well.
In every zone, a tale card has only its normal characteristics.
If an effect instructs a player to choose a card name and the player wants to choose a tale card’s alternative name, the player may do so.

formal_source_nodes.name: 111.10am
formal_source_nodes.rule: A Function token with (effect) is a colorless Function enchantment token with “You may sacrifice this Function as you cast an instant or sorcery spell. If you do, that spell gains (effect).”

subrules.name: 303.8a
subrules.rule:
Each Function has an ability that can add effects to an instant or sorcery spell. The Function itself does not have these abilities, but rather an ability that grants them.
Example: Bastion Chaplain says "When Bastion Chaplain enters, create two Function tokens with 'Lifelink.'" The Function tokens do not have lifelink themselves.

subrules.name: 303.8b
subrules.rule: As a player is casting an instant or sorcery spell, they may sacrifice any Functions they control to add their effects to that spell. If a player controls any Functions which could give the spell flash or let the spell be cast as though it had flash, they may begin to cast that spell as though it had flash (see rule 601.3b).

subrules.name: 303.8c
subrules.rule: The spell has the characteristics of the main spell, plus the rules text granted by each of the Functions. This is a text-changing effect (see rule 612, “Text-Changing Effects”). The spell doesn’t gain any other characteristics (name, mana cost, color, supertypes, card types, subtypes, wu xing number, etc.) of the Function cards. Text gained by the spell that refers to a card by name refers to the spell on the stack, not the card from which the text was copied.

subrules.name: 303.8d
subrules.rule:
A Function's effects are added to a spell after alternate and additional costs have been selected for a spell. Any alternate or additional costs provided by the Function will be present on the spell but unable to be used.
Example: If a Function gives a spell kicker {1}, that spell will have kicker, but this kicker cost could not be paid.

subrules.name: 303.8e
subrules.rule:
Some cards create a Function "with the effects" of an instant or sorcery spell, activated ability, or triggered ability. The Function will remember choices made during the process in rule 601.2b, and costs paid for the original spell or ability, and apply them to the effects granted by the Function. In particular, it will retain which modes were selected, the value for X of the original spell, and Functions that were added to that spell, and it will not retain targets and divisions or distributions. Unselected modes will still be added to the spell, and may be selected if an effect allows the spell's modes to be reselected. These only apply to the text added by the Function, and not the rest of the spell.
Example: Beckon the Shadows says "Bloodprice {2}{B}{B}" and its effect checks if it was cast for its bloodprice. These effects added by a Function will only be considered as cast for its bloodprice if the original spell was, and it does not impact abilities of other Functions or the new spell being cast checking if they were cast for its bloodprice. The new spell cannot be cast for bloodprice {2}{B}{B} this way. If any bloodprice is paid, casting the spell is still considered "casting a spell for its bloodprice."
Example: Swords Dance says "Harness" and its spell effect applies to "the creature that harnessed it". If a new spell is cast, it will not be able to tap additional creatures to reduce its cost. If the harness cost of the original spell was paid, that same reduction will be applied to the new spell, and "the creature that harnessed it" will still be remembered, if that object is still on the battlefield.
Example: A Function with the effects of a spell with glitch will remember which words were removed from the text, and the spell will be a "glitched spell" if any were removed. If the new spell being cast has glitch, words from the Function cannot be removed with that ability.

subrules.name: 303.8f
subrules.rule:
Functions do not change what kind of card the spell they are attached to are. Rules that describe how the textboxes of alternate card kinds work only apply to the individual Function effect added to the spell.
Example: A Function with the effects of a Wu Xing card will grant effects for its effects equal to the wu xing number of the original spell. The effects are not determined by the wu xing number of the spell, if it has one, and the Function's wu xing number does not become the spell's wu xing number.
Example: Second Death is a sorcery with an Adventure, First Death. If a Function with the effects of a spell that was cast as an Adventure is added onto it, Second Death will be cast as an Adventure, but will remain Second Death, not First Death. Second Death will be exiled after it resolves, and can be cast from exile as long as it isn't cast as an Adventure, including both casting First Death, or adding another Function that was cast as an Adventure onto it.
Example: A Function with the effects of a spell with fabled will only be able to be transformed and put onto the battlefield attached to a permanent the back face of that card can enchant. If a spell has multiple instances of fabled, its controller chooses which will apply as it resolves.
Example: A Function with the effects of a spell with coalesce that was paid will put the card onto the battlefield as a Horror creature. If that card does not have a power and toughness, it will be 0/0, rather than the power and toughness of the original spell with coalesce.

subrules.name: 303.8g
subrules.rule: Effects may identify individual Functions applied to a spell, which includes all effects added by that Function and all choices it retained.

formal_source_nodes.name: 601.2b
formal_source_nodes.rule: If the spell is modal, the player announces the mode choice (see rule 700.2). If the player making the mode choice needs to be targeted, the player casting the spell announces their choice of an appropriate player for each target required to make that choice, and only those targets, at this time instead of the normal time during 601.2c. If the number of choices has a currently undefined value, such as “Choose X,” or a value that may change during the process of casting the spell, such as “If this spell was kicked, choose any number instead”, the player chooses any number of modes. When the spell's legality is checked (rule 601.2e), if the value is still undefined or the value does not match the choices originally made, the spell is illegal. If the player wishes to splice any cards onto the spell (see rule 702.46), they reveal those cards in their hand. If that player wishes to reprise any cards onto that spell (see rule 702.205), they exile those cards from their graveyard. If the player wishes to apply any Functions to that spell (see rule 111.10aj), they sacrifice those Functions. If the player wishes to apply any any modes from exiled cards with lucid (see rule 702.304), they put those cards into their owner's graveyard. They choose an order to apply those text-change effects to that spell. If the spell has alternative or additional costs that will be paid as it's being cast such as buyback or kicker costs (see rules 118.8 and 118.9), the player announces their intentions to pay any or all of those costs (see rule 601.2f). A player can't apply two alternative methods of casting or two alternative costs to a single spell. If the spell has a variable cost that will be paid as it's being cast (such as an {X} in its mana cost; see rule 107.3), the player announces the value of that variable. If the value of that variable is defined in the text of the spell by a choice that player would make later in the announcement or resolution of the spell, that player makes that choice at this time instead of that later time. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast includes hybrid mana symbols, the player announces the nonhybrid equivalent cost they intend to pay. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast includes Phyrexian mana symbols, the player announces whether they intend to pay 2 life or a corresponding colored mana cost for each of those symbols. Previously made choices (such as choosing to cast a spell with flashback from a graveyard or choosing to cast a creature with morph face down) may restrict the player's options when making these choices.

subrules.name: 702.304a
subrules.rule: Lucid appears on some modal instant and sorceries. It represents a static ability that functions while the spell is on the stack. "Lucid" means "If you cast this spell from your hand or from exile, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else as it resolves. As you cast a modal instant or sorcery spell while this card is exiled, you may choose one of this card's modes. If you do, change the text of that spell by adding the chosen mode into one of its bulleted lists and put this card into its owner's graveyard."

subrules.name: 702.304b
subrules.rule: If you're applying more than one card with lucid onto a spell, you will put them all into their owner's graveyard and choose the order in which the effects will happen. The new modes will always be added to the end of the list.

subrules.name: 702.304c
subrules.rule: The spell has the characteristics of the main spell, plus the rules text found in the chosen mode of the lucid card. This is a text-changing effect (see rule 612, “Text-Changing Effects”). The spell doesn’t gain any other characteristics (name, mana cost, color, supertypes, card types, subtypes, etc.) of the lucid cards. Text gained by the spell that refers to a card by name refers to the spell on the stack, not the card from which the text was copied.

subrules.name: 702.304d
subrules.rule: If a mode with an associated cost, such as those found on cards with spree, is added to another spell, this cost will still need to be paid regardless if the new spell has spree.

subrules.name: 702.304e
subrules.rule: If a mode without an associated cost is added to a card with spree, the player will be unable to pay its associated cost and unable to choose the mode.

subrules.name: 702.304f
subrules.rule: If a mode with star or pawprint symbols is added to a modal spell which does not use them to select modes, the mode may be chosen regardless of those symbols.

subrules.name: 702.304g
subrules.rule: If a mode without stars or pawprints is added to a modal spell that does use them to select modes, the mode is not a legal choice.

subrules.name: 702.223a
subrules.rule: Chant is a static ability that functions while a card is in your hand. “Chant [cost]” means “You may exile this card from your hand as you cast an instant or sorcery spell. If you do, that spell gains the text found within square brackets in this card’s rules text and you pay [cost] as an additional cost to cast that spell. You may cast this card as long as this card remains exiled.” Paying a card’s chant cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.223b
subrules.rule: Some effect may allow a player to "add the chants" of cards to spells they cast. To do so, they choose the cards with chant that will add their chants. The spell gains the text found within the square brackets in those card's rules text, and that player pays [cost] as an additional cost to cast that spell. The chanting creatures will not be exiled.

subrules.name: 702.223c
subrules.rule: You can’t choose to use a chant ability if you can’t make the required choices (targets, etc.) for that card’s rules text. If you’re chanting more than one card onto a spell, exile them all at once and choose the order in which their effects will happen. The effects of the main spell must happen first.

subrules.name: 702.223d
subrules.rule: The spell has the characteristics of the main spell, plus the rules text found in the square brackets of each of the chanting cards. This is a text-changing effect (see rule 612, “Text-Changing Effects”). The spell doesn’t gain any other characteristics (name, mana cost, color, supertypes, card types, subtypes, etc.) of the chanting cards. Text gained by the spell that refers to a card by name refers to the spell on the stack, not the card from which the text was copied.

subrules.name: 702.223e
subrules.rule: Choose targets for the added text normally (see rule 601.2c). Note that a spell with one or more targets won’t resolve if all of its targets are illegal on resolution.

subrules.name: 702.223f
subrules.rule: The spell loses any chant changes once it leaves the stack for any reason.
